name: ssid.ai router default-credential dataset
description: Default login IP, username, password (or an explicit reason there is none), credential type, and factory-reset steps for consumer routers, gateways, mesh systems and access points. Every row cites the manufacturer's own documentation.

routers.credential_note: Verizon's official Actiontec manual documents the default login as admin / password, after which the router forces you to choose your own credentials. Be aware later revisions (rev C/D and many field-installed FiOS units) instead use a unique password derived from the serial number and printed on the device label.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser to http://192.168.1.1 and log in with admin / password; the router then prompts you to set your own username and password. If that fails, press and hold the Reset button on the back for about 10-15 seconds until it reboots. Note: many FiOS units use a unique password printed on the label instead — check the sticker if admin/password is rejected.
routers.source_name: Verizon Actiontec Router User Manual (official PDF)

routers.credential_note: Airtel's official support page documents 192.168.1.1 with admin / password as the login. This is a genuinely documented default, not an invented admin/admin. Airtel ships several ODM units (Nokia, ZTE, Syrotech); newer fibre ONTs increasingly carry a unique admin password printed on the device label, so check the sticker if admin/password does not work.
routers.reset_steps: Connect to the router over Wi-Fi or by LAN cable, open http://192.168.1.1 in a browser, and sign in with username admin and password password (Airtel's documented default). To factory reset, press and hold the recessed RESET button on the back for about 10-15 seconds until the LEDs blink and the unit reboots, then log back in at 192.168.1.1. If admin/password is rejected, check the sticker on the underside of the unit for a per-device password.
routers.source_name: Airtel — Use IP address to login to router settings

routers.credential_note: App-only: the network cannot be configured through a web browser. Login uses a one-time code by SMS/email (or a linked Amazon account) — no default username, password, or admin IP.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the reset button on the back ~15 seconds until the LED flashes red for a full factory reset (erases all network config).
routers.source_name: eero Help Center — Do I need a password to log in?

routers.credential_note: The password is derived from the device: username admin, password = last 8 digits of the serial number printed on the label, with a forced password change on first login. Some early firmware accepted admin/password. No universal factory default.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser to http://192.168.100.1 to reach the S33 web manager (this is a cable-modem diagnostics/settings page, not a Wi-Fi router). Log in with username 'admin' and the last 8 digits of the serial number on the bottom label, then create a new password when prompted. If locked out, wait 10 minutes after too many failed attempts, or factory reset by holding the recessed Reset button on the back for about 10 seconds; after reset, log in again with admin + last 8 of the serial.
routers.source_name: ARRIS SURFboard Support (S33/S34: Web Manager Access)

routers.credential_note: Modem, not a router. Older firmware shipped with admin/password, but current firmware uses admin plus the last 8 digits of the serial number (from the label) and forces you to create a new password on first login. There is no universal admin/admin.
routers.reset_steps: The SB8200 is a modem only (no Wi-Fi), so 192.168.100.1 is a diagnostics/web-manager page, not a router settings page. To reach it, open a browser to http://192.168.100.1. On current firmware the username is 'admin' and the password is the last 8 characters of the serial number printed on the modem's bottom label; you'll be prompted to set a new password on first login. To factory reset, press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back with a paperclip for about 10 seconds until the modem restarts, which reverts the admin password to the last-8-of-serial default.
routers.source_name: ARRIS SURFboard Support (SB8200: Web Manager Access)

routers.credential_note: Documented default is admin / password (case-sensitive); the web UI forces you to change username and password on first login.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the recessed reset button on the rear ~15 seconds until the modem restarts to restore factory defaults.
routers.source_name: ARRIS SURFboard official support (SBG7600AC2 user guide)

routers.credential_note: No universal default credentials. The AP is managed entirely via an Instant On account you create; the account password (not admin/admin) is your login.
routers.reset_steps: The Instant On AP11 is configured through the HPE Networking Instant On mobile app (or web app). Install the app, choose 'Create an account', register with your own email and a self-chosen password, verify by email, then let the app find and set up the AP — no built-in admin password exists. To factory reset, with the AP powered on press and hold the Reset button for about 1–15 seconds until the LED signals a reset, then re-onboard it in the app.
routers.source_name: HPE Networking Instant On 3.1.0 User Guide

routers.credential_note: No default admin/admin. Access is via an Instant On cloud account you create (your email + your chosen password); the same account manages the AP locally and remotely.
routers.reset_steps: The Instant On AP22 is set up through the HPE Networking Instant On mobile app (or the web app at instant-on.hpe.com). Install the app, tap 'Create an account', register with your own email and a password you choose, verify by email, then follow the app to discover and configure the AP — there is no factory admin password. To factory reset, with the AP powered on hold the Reset button for about 1–15 seconds until the LED indicates reset, then re-add it in the app.
routers.source_name: HPE Networking Instant On 3.1.0 User Guide

routers.credential_note: Gaming router firmware requires setting your own admin password at setup. Login name defaults to 'admin'; there is no fixed default password.
routers.reset_steps: The Quick Internet Setup wizard forces you to create your own admin login name and password on first login — no admin/admin default. To factory reset: with the router on, press and hold the RESET button (rear) for 5-10 seconds until the power LED flashes, release, and wait for reboot. Re-run setup at http://router.asus.com (192.168.50.1) and set a new admin password.
routers.source_name: ASUS Official Support — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI?

routers.credential_note: The ROG Rapture GT-AXE16000 is a WiFi 6E (AXE16000) flagship, and like every current ASUS it has no factory password: setup forces you to pick one. The account name starts out as admin.
routers.reset_steps: Setup on first login compels you to create your own admin login and password — nothing is shipped preset. Factory reset: with the router on, hold the rear RESET button 5-10 seconds until the power LED flashes, release, and let it come back up. Re-run setup at http://router.asus.com (192.168.50.1) and pick a new admin password.
routers.source_name: ASUS Official Support — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI?

routers.credential_note: Older model with login name 'admin'; early firmware used password 'admin', but current firmware forces you to set your own password on first setup. Don't rely on admin/admin. Default IP is 192.168.1.1.
routers.reset_steps: On current firmware the Quick Internet Setup wizard requires you to create your own admin login and password. To factory reset: with the router on, hold the rear RESET button 5-10 seconds until the power LED flashes, release, and wait for reboot. Then browse to http://router.asus.com (192.168.1.1) and set a new admin password.
routers.source_name: ASUS Official Support — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI?

routers.credential_note: Older model historically ships admin / admin. Recent firmware also prompts you to set a login on first setup, so on updated units the password may be user-set.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the hardware Reset button for at least 5 seconds until the power LED starts to flash.
routers.source_name: ASUS official Support FAQ 1005263

routers.credential_note: This older model historically shipped with login name 'admin' and, on early firmware, password 'admin' — but current firmware forces you to set your own password during setup. Treat 'admin/admin' as not reliable; set your own. Default IP is 192.168.1.1 on this generation.
routers.reset_steps: On current firmware the setup wizard forces you to create your own admin login and password on first login. To factory reset: with the router on, press and hold the RESET button (rear) for 5-10 seconds until the power LED flashes, release, and wait for reboot. Then browse to http://router.asus.com (192.168.1.1) and set a new admin password.
routers.source_name: ASUS Official Support — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI?

routers.credential_note: AX3000 dual-band WiFi 6. No fixed password ships with the RT-AX3000; you define one during the initial setup pass. The account name it begins with is admin.
routers.reset_steps: Whether it is a brand-new unit or one just reset, the setup wizard requires a self-created admin login and password — no default is provided. Factory reset: power on, press and hold RESET at the rear for 5-10 seconds until the power LED flashes, release, and let it reboot. Then set a new admin password from http://router.asus.com (192.168.50.1).
routers.source_name: ASUS Official Support — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI?

routers.credential_note: ASUS forces you to create a login account + password on first setup / after a factory reset. Legacy default account name is admin.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button on the back for at least 5 seconds until the power LED starts flashing.
routers.source_name: ASUS official Support FAQ 1005263

routers.credential_note: AX2700-class Wi-Fi 6 router (3x3 80MHz dual-band, 4 external antennas, AiMesh support) — distinct SKU from the RT-AX3000 (a rebadged RT-AX58U) already covered. Official FAQ: on first login (or after factory reset) you must set the router login account and password yourself; there is no admin/admin.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the WPS/Reset button on the rear panel for more than 5 seconds until the power LED flashes, then release to restore factory default settings.
routers.source_name: ASUS official FAQ — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI? (applies to RT-AX68U)

routers.credential_note: RT-AX82U: WiFi 6, reached at router.asus.com or 192.168.50.1. ASUS ships nothing preset — the initial wizard demands an account name and password of your own. The account name starts as admin.
routers.reset_steps: First access runs Quick Internet Setup, which requires you to invent both the admin account name and its password; there is no factory pair to fall back on. Factory reset: with power applied, press the RESET button on the rear for 5-10 seconds until the power LED blinks, let go, and let it restart. Re-run the wizard at http://router.asus.com (192.168.50.1) to pick a new password.
routers.source_name: ASUS Official Support — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI?

routers.credential_note: Current firmware requires you to set your own admin password during setup. The account name defaults to 'admin', but there is no fixed default password.
routers.reset_steps: On first login or after a reset, the Quick Internet Setup wizard forces you to create your own admin login name and password — no admin/admin default. To factory reset: with the router on, press and hold the RESET button (rear, near the WAN port) for 5-10 seconds until the power LED flashes, release, and wait for reboot. Then browse to http://router.asus.com (192.168.50.1) and set a new admin password.
routers.source_name: ASUS Official Support — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI?

routers.credential_note: On the RT-AX86U Pro there is no admin/admin. The firmware stops at a create-your-credentials screen the first time you connect. Its starting login name is admin, and the password is only ever the one you typed.
routers.reset_steps: The wizard on first login makes you build your own admin login and password, so no factory password is documented. To restore defaults: with the unit running, hold RESET at the back 5-10 seconds until the power LED flashes, release, and allow the reboot. Set the admin password once more via http://router.asus.com (192.168.50.1).
routers.source_name: ASUS Official Support — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI?

routers.credential_note: ASUS forces creating a login account + password during initial QIS setup / after factory reset. Legacy default account name is admin.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button on the back for at least 5 seconds until the power LED starts flashing, then release.
routers.source_name: ASUS official Support FAQ 1005263

routers.credential_note: Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) BE6800 dual-band router with SMB/UPnP-AV/FTP file sharing, desktop form factor with external antennas — a step below the dual-10G RT-BE88U in this run. On first setup ASUS forces a login: "change the router's login password to prevent unauthorized access to your wireless router."
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the recessed Reset button on the rear until the power LED flashes (about 5-10 seconds), then complete the Quick Internet Setup (QIS) to set a new login.
routers.source_name: ASUS RT-BE86U User Guide (E25474) — official PDF

routers.credential_note: Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) BE7200 dual-band 4x4 prosumer router with dual 10 Gbps ports (WAN/LAN + SFP+), quad 2.5 Gbps LAN and USB 3.2 Gen1 — a wired-heavy tier distinct from the RT-BE96U already covered. No admin/admin: ASUS forces you to set the login during first setup — "change the router's login password to prevent unauthorized access to your wireless router."
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the recessed Reset button on the rear until the power LED starts flashing (about 5-10 seconds), then re-run the Quick Internet Setup (QIS) to create a new login.
routers.source_name: ASUS RT-BE88U User Guide (E23805) — official PDF

routers.credential_note: BE19000 WiFi 7 flagship. No factory admin/admin — AsusWRT makes you set the login account and password during first setup at router.asus.com (192.168.50.1) or via the ASUS Router app. admin is the conventional login name.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button on the back at least 5 seconds until the power LED flashes, then release; on the Quick Internet Setup that follows you create the router login account and password.
routers.source_name: ASUS official Support FAQ 1005263

routers.credential_note: AX3000 dual-band WiFi 6 gaming router. Same AsusWRT model: no preset password, you create the login account on first setup (router.asus.com / 192.168.50.1 or the ASUS Router app). Behavior per ASUS's general router FAQ.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold Reset at least 5 seconds until the power LED blinks, release to factory-reset, then complete Quick Internet Setup where you choose the admin login and password.
routers.source_name: ASUS official Support FAQ 1005263

routers.credential_note: The TUF Gaming AX5400 is WiFi 6 hardware and it ships with no usable password. Quick Internet Setup will not complete until you supply your own; the login name it starts from is admin.
routers.reset_steps: No default exists because QIS forces a self-chosen admin login name and password at first access. For a factory reset, keep the rear RESET button held 5-10 seconds with the router on, until the power LED flashes; release and wait out the reboot. Then re-run QIS at http://router.asus.com (192.168.50.1) and choose the admin password again.
routers.source_name: ASUS Official Support — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI?

routers.credential_note: Modern ZenWiFi firmware forces you to create your own admin password during first setup — there is no admin/admin default. The account NAME defaults to 'admin', but the password is whatever you set.
routers.reset_steps: During ASUS Router app or web setup (Quick Internet Setup), you create your own admin login name and password — there is no fixed default password. To factory reset: with the node powered on, press and hold the RESET button (recessed, next to the ports on the back) for 5-10 seconds until the power LED starts flashing, then release and wait for it to reboot. Re-run setup via the ASUS Router app or by browsing to http://router.asus.com (192.168.50.1) and create a new admin password.
routers.source_name: ASUS Official Support — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI?

routers.credential_note: XD4 is app-first mesh but still exposes the web GUI; either way you must set your own admin password on first setup. No admin/admin default. Account name defaults to 'admin'.
routers.reset_steps: Initial setup through the ASUS Router app forces you to create your own admin login and password — no default password ships. To factory reset a node: power it on, press and hold the RESET button on the bottom for 5-10 seconds until the LED flashes, release, and wait for reboot. Re-run setup at http://router.asus.com (192.168.50.1) to set a new admin password.
routers.source_name: ASUS Official Support — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI?

routers.credential_note: Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) BE3600 dual-band AiMesh whole-home mesh system with two auto-sensing 2.5GbE ports per node — the Wi-Fi 7 entry tier below the ZenWiFi BQ16 already covered. Web setup redirects to the ASUS QIS wizard where the owner creates the login; ASUS: "Login name and password are required when accessing to router configuration page."
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button on the rear of a node until the LED indicates a reset, then re-run setup via a web browser (redirects to the ASUS Setup Wizard) or the ASUS Router App to create a new login.
routers.source_name: ASUS official Support FAQ 1016107 (QIS setup)

routers.credential_note: BE3600 dual-band Wi-Fi 7 outdoor (IP65-rated) mesh node with 2.5GbE PoE — a weatherproof SKU with its own manual (E25876), distinct from the indoor ZenWiFi BD4 already covered. No default password; QIS forces you to set the login name and password on first setup. ASUS: "Set up a password for your router to prevent unauthorized access."
routers.reset_steps: Press the Reset button to restore factory defaults, then complete Quick Internet Setup (QIS), which forces a new login username and password.
routers.source_name: ASUS ZenWiFi BD4 Outdoor User Guide (official, E25876)

routers.credential_note: This tri-band mesh forces you to create your own admin password on first login — there is no admin/admin default. Account name defaults to 'admin'.
routers.reset_steps: During first setup (ASUS Router app or Quick Internet Setup) you create your own admin login and password — nothing ships pre-set. To factory reset: power the node on, press and hold the RESET button 5-10 seconds until the power LED flashes, release, and wait for reboot. Re-run setup at http://router.asus.com (192.168.50.1) to define a new admin password.
routers.source_name: ASUS Official Support — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI?

routers.credential_note: AXE6600 tri-band Wi-Fi 6E mesh (2.4 + 5 + 6 GHz; 6 GHz up to 4804 Mbps) with a 2.5G WAN port. No universal default password — the web login credentials are created during first-time QIS; the legacy default account name is admin. ASUS: "Set up a password for your router to prevent unauthorized access."
routers.reset_steps: Hold the rear Reset button until the power LED flashes to restore defaults; Quick Internet Setup (QIS) then runs again and makes you set a new login name and password.
routers.source_name: ASUS ZenWiFi ET8 User Guide (official, E19334)

routers.credential_note: No admin/admin default — firmware forces a password on first login. Login name defaults to 'admin'.
routers.reset_steps: Quick Internet Setup (web or ASUS Router app) requires you to create your own admin login name and password — no default password. To factory reset: with the unit on, hold the rear RESET button 5-10 seconds until the power LED flashes, then release and let it reboot. Re-run setup at http://router.asus.com (192.168.50.1) and set a new admin password.
routers.source_name: ASUS Official Support — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI?

routers.credential_note: Firmware requires creating your own admin password on first login; there is no universal admin/admin. Login name defaults to 'admin'.
routers.reset_steps: Setup (ASUS Router app or Quick Internet Setup) makes you choose your own admin login name and password — no fixed default. To factory reset: power the node on, press and hold the rear RESET button 5-10 seconds until the power LED flashes, release, and let it reboot. Re-run setup at http://router.asus.com (192.168.50.1) and set a new admin password.
routers.source_name: ASUS Official Support — How do I enter my ASUS router's setting page using Web GUI?

routers.credential_note: The BGW210 uses a per-device 'Device Access Code' on the label, not a shared password. Older third-party lists cite 'attadmin', but current units authenticate only with the unique code printed on the gateway.
routers.reset_steps: Browse to http://192.168.1.254. No username is required; enter the Device Access Code from the sticker on the side/bottom of the BGW210 when prompted to change settings. To restore factory defaults and reset the access code, press and hold the recessed Reset button ~10 seconds (hold ~15-20 seconds for a full reset), then authorize using the label's Device Access Code.
routers.source_name: AT&T Internet Support — Change Your Wi-Fi Gateway Access Code

routers.credential_note: AT&T gateways have no admin username and no shared default password. The single credential is the per-device 'Device Access Code' printed on the gateway label — each unit is different, so no universal default exists.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser to http://192.168.1.254 to reach the gateway UI. There is no username; when a setting asks for authorization, enter the Device Access Code printed on the sticker on the side of the BGW320 (a unique alphanumeric string). To reset the access code, press and hold the recessed Reset button on the side for ~10 seconds; a longer 15-20 second hold performs a full factory reset. After reset, use the Device Access Code printed on the label.
routers.source_name: AT&T Internet Support — Change Your Wi-Fi Gateway Access Code

routers.credential_note: AT&T's 2Wire/Pace/BGW/NVG gateways do not use admin/admin — each unit has a unique Device Access Code printed on a sticker on the gateway. AT&T's official support confirms the code lives on the device label and is reset to that label value by a factory reset.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser to http://192.168.1.254 to reach the Gateway User Interface. When asked for a Device Access Code, enter the code printed on the sticker on the side or bottom of the gateway. To reset, press and hold the Reset button for about 10 seconds until the gateway restarts; the access code reverts to the one on the label.
routers.source_name: AT&T Support — Gateway User Interface for Wi-Fi gateways

routers.credential_note: The FRITZ!Box 4060 is a pure tri-band Wi-Fi 6 router with no modem and no telephone ports. Its factory password is unique per device and printed on the underside label; enter it at http://fritz.box (192.168.178.1). There is no username and no admin/admin default.
routers.reset_steps: Because the 4060 has no phone ports, reset it from the interface: System > Backup > Load Factory Settings, then confirm and wait for the WLAN LED to stay lit.
routers.source_name: AVM official FRITZ!Box 4060 knowledge base #3531

routers.credential_note: The FRITZ!Box 5590 Fiber is an AON/GPON fibre gateway with Wi-Fi 6 and telephony. Like other current FRITZ!Box models it carries a unique password on the base type label rather than a shared default, entered at http://fritz.box (192.168.178.1); there is no username.
routers.reset_steps: Use System > Backup > Load Factory Settings in the interface and confirm, or dial #991*15901590* on an attached phone and hang up after about three seconds, to restore factory defaults.
routers.source_name: AVM official FRITZ!Box 5590 Fiber knowledge base #3531

routers.credential_note: DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem router with FRITZ!Mesh support (as Master or Repeater) — distinct from the DSL/fibre FRITZ!Box models already covered. Login password is a unique per-device string printed on the type label on the bottom of the housing, not a shared default, per AVM's own knowledge base.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button on the rear panel for about 5 seconds, or use System > Backup > Restore Factory Settings in the FRITZ!OS user interface.
routers.source_name: AVM FRITZ! Knowledge Base — Opening/Determining the password for the FRITZ!Box user interface (FRITZ!Box 6591 Cable) (official)

routers.credential_note: The FRITZ!Box 6660 Cable is a DOCSIS 3.1 cable gateway with Wi-Fi 6. It has no default admin/admin: the per-unit password is printed on the type label on the base and typed into http://fritz.box (192.168.178.1). Login is password-only.
routers.reset_steps: Restore defaults from System > Backup > Load Factory Settings in the FRITZ!OS interface, or dial #991*15901590* from a connected telephone and hang up after about three seconds.
routers.source_name: AVM official FRITZ!Box 6660 Cable knowledge base #3531

routers.credential_note: The FRITZ!Box 7490 is an older VDSL/ADSL flagship. Unlike current models it ships with NO password at all — on the first visit to http://fritz.box (192.168.178.1) you must set your own. There is still no username field and no admin/admin default.
routers.reset_steps: Assign your own password on the first visit. To factory-reset, use System > Backup > Load Factory Settings in the interface, or dial #991*15901590* from an attached telephone and hang up after about three seconds.
routers.source_name: AVM official FRITZ!Box 7490 knowledge base #3531

routers.credential_note: The FRITZ!Box 7530 is a compact VDSL/ADSL router with DECT telephony. AVM ships it with a per-device user-interface password on the underside type label (no admin/admin, no username); type it in at http://fritz.box or 192.168.178.1.
routers.reset_steps: In the FRITZ!OS interface choose System > Backup > Load Factory Settings and confirm; alternatively dial #991*15901590* from a connected phone and hang up after a few seconds.
routers.source_name: AVM official FRITZ!Box 7530 knowledge base #3531

routers.credential_note: The 7530 AX adds Wi-Fi 6 to AVM's popular compact 7530 DSL router. Its user interface is protected by a unique factory password printed on the device label — not a universal default — and is reached at http://fritz.box (192.168.178.1) with a password only.
routers.reset_steps: Factory-reset from System > Backup > Load Factory Settings in the interface, or from a connected telephone dial #991*15901590* and hang up after roughly three seconds.
routers.source_name: AVM official FRITZ!Box 7530 AX knowledge base #3531

routers.credential_note: The FRITZ!Box 7583 is a VDSL supervectoring (35b) router aimed at long lines and small-business use, with DECT and telephony. It ships with a unique label password (no shared default, no username) used at http://fritz.box or 192.168.178.1.
routers.reset_steps: Reset via System > Backup > Load Factory Settings in the interface, or by dialling #991*15901590* on a connected phone and hanging up after a few seconds.
routers.source_name: AVM official FRITZ!Box 7583 knowledge base #3531

routers.credential_note: The FRITZ!Box 7590 is AVM's flagship VDSL/ADSL router with a built-in DECT base and analog/ISDN telephony. There is no admin/admin: each unit ships with its own password (4–6 lower-case letters then 4 digits) printed on the type label underneath, entered at http://fritz.box (192.168.178.1) with no username.
routers.reset_steps: Open the interface and choose System > Backup > Load Factory Settings and confirm — the LEDs flash once and the WLAN LED stays lit when finished. On a connected phone you can instead dial #991*15901590* and hang up after about three seconds.
routers.source_name: AVM official FRITZ!Box 7590 knowledge base #3531

routers.credential_note: The 7590 AX is the Wi-Fi 6 (AX) revision of AVM's 7590 DSL flagship. Login is password-only at http://fritz.box (192.168.178.1): the factory password is unique to the device and printed on its base label, so there is no shared default and no username field.
routers.reset_steps: Reset from the interface via System > Backup > Load Factory Settings (confirm, then the WLAN LED stays lit), or dial #991*15901590* on an attached telephone and hang up after roughly three seconds.
routers.source_name: AVM official FRITZ!Box 7590 AX knowledge base #3531

routers.credential_note: Per Belkin's official support, these routers ship with the admin dashboard unlocked — there is no default password at all (both fields blank). You optionally click the lock icon to set one. This is why aggregators listing admin/admin for Belkin are wrong.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser to http://192.168.2.1 (or http://router). By default the dashboard opens without a password — leave the username and password blank and submit. To factory reset, press and hold the Reset button on the bottom for about 10-15 seconds until the lights blink, then release; the dashboard returns to no-password (unlocked).
routers.source_name: Belkin Official Support — Accessing 192.168.2.1

routers.model: Legacy N & AC routers (192.168.2.1 models, e.g. F9K/N600/N750)
routers.credential_note: Belkin Official Support states these older Belkin routers 'don't have default passwords' — the admin password is blank out of the box, so you log in by clicking Login then Submit. There is no admin/admin. Set a password after logging in.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button for about 10 seconds to restore factory defaults (this erases current settings). Open a browser and go to http://192.168.2.1 (or http://router). Click Login and then Submit, leaving the password blank — older Belkin routers ship with no default password.
routers.source_name: Belkin Official Support — Accessing 192.168.2.1 (default password / login)

routers.credential_note: Belkin officially lists the RT1800 default password as 'admin' with no username, and default IP 192.168.1.1 — this is a genuine documented static default, so change it immediately after setup.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button for about 10 seconds until the router restarts to factory defaults. If the setup wizard closes on a Mac, install manually: browse to http://192.168.1.1 and log in with the default password 'admin'. Default WiFi names are BelkinXXXXX and BelkinXXXXX_5GHz (XXXXX = last five digits of the serial); the default guest password is 'guest'.
routers.source_name: Belkin Official Support — RT1800 setup / default settings

routers.credential_note: Belkin's own RT3200 user guide states the default parent-router password is 'admin' (no username). It is meant to be changed during setup; treat 'admin' only as the untouched factory value.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button on the back/bottom for about 10 seconds (or use the Administration tab in the router's settings) to restore factory defaults. Browse to http://myrouter.local (or http://192.168.1.1) and log in — the user guide states the default password is 'admin' if you skipped setup or never changed it.
routers.source_name: Belkin Official Support — RT3200 User Guide (PDF)

routers.credential_note: Canadian fibre/FTTH gateway. Admin is reached at bell.ca/mymodem (when connected) or 192.168.2.1. There is no default username, and the default administrator password is the modem's own serial number printed on the sticker on the back of the unit — a unique per-device value, not a generic default.
routers.reset_steps: Perform a factory reset (hold the reset button on the modem) to restore the default admin password, which is the serial number on the back-panel sticker. On-device, use the front up/down arrows to select Modem Management to view settings.
routers.source_name: Bell Official Support — Set or change the administrator password (Home Hub 4000)

routers.credential_note: Bell's tri-band Wi-Fi 6 fibre gateway (XGS-PON/GPON FTTH, supports Bell Home phone/VoIP). Admin login is password-only with no username field; the default password is the unit's serial number from the rear label — unique per device, not a shared static default. Distinct from the older Home Hub 4000.
routers.reset_steps: Browse to bell.ca/mymodem (or 192.168.2.1) and log in with the administrator password, which by default is the serial number printed on the sticker on the back of the modem. To wipe a custom password, hold the recessed reset button on the back until the modem restarts.
routers.source_name: Bell Support — Managing my Giga Hub modem (official)

routers.credential_note: Applies to Axon C4000BG/LG/XG and Zyxel C4000BZ/LZ. Brightspeed provisions a unique admin username and password on each modem's sticker — there is no shared default, and the preset values cannot be retrieved if the sticker is lost.
routers.reset_steps: Browse to http://192.168.0.1 to open the modem GUI. Log in with the Admin Username and Admin Password on the sticker attached to the side/back/bottom of the modem (unique per device; different from the WiFi network name/key). To factory reset, press and hold the recessed Reset button ~10-15 seconds until it reboots, then sign in with the label's default Admin credentials.
routers.source_name: Brightspeed — Administrator Password, Advanced Modem Setup

routers.credential_note: BSNL's official circle support page documents http://192.168.1.1 with admin / admin for this legacy ADSL modem. Note that BSNL Bharat Fibre (FTTH) hands out Nokia/ZTE/Syrotech GPON ONTs instead, which are provisioned by BSNL and usually carry a per-device admin password on the label rather than admin/admin.
routers.reset_steps: Connect to the modem by LAN or Wi-Fi, open http://192.168.1.1 in a browser, and sign in with username admin and password admin (BSNL's documented default). Configure the PPPoE connection with the broadband username/password given by BSNL, then set WPA-PSK wireless security. To factory reset, hold the recessed RESET button for about 10 seconds until the modem reboots, then log back in at 192.168.1.1.
routers.source_name: BSNL Chennai Telephones — Modem Configuration / Wireless Security

routers.credential_note: There is no admin/admin default. Each BT Smart Hub 2 ships with a unique admin password printed on the pull-out settings card on the back (or the base label). The admin password is separate from the WiFi key.
routers.reset_steps: To log in: connect to the hub, open a browser and go to bthomehub.home or 192.168.1.254, then enter the admin password. The admin password is on the pull-out settings card on the back of the hub (and on the base label). It is not your WiFi key. To factory reset: with the hub powered on, press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back for about 20 seconds until the lights flash; the hub reboots and all settings, including the admin password, revert to those printed on the card.
routers.source_name: BT Help — Set up or change the admin password on my BT Hub

routers.credential_note: Buffalo's official AirStation manual documents the genuine factory default as username 'admin' / password 'password' at 192.168.11.1 — one of the few brands with a real universal default. The initial settings are also printed on the AirStation setup card stored in the base. Change the password after logging in.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button until the AirStation reinitializes to factory defaults. In router mode browse to http://192.168.11.1 (in bridge/access-point mode use http://192.168.11.100); if a login prompt appears, enter username 'admin' and password 'password', click Log In, and step through the wizard.
routers.source_name: Buffalo — AirStation WHR-1166D User Manual (PDF, manual.buffalo.jp)

routers.credential_note: Buffalo's AirStation web interface uses the series-wide factory default admin / password at 192.168.11.1 (documented in Buffalo's official AirStation manuals); the initial login is also printed on the AirStation setup card in the base. Change it after first login.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button until the diagnostic LED flashes and the AirStation restores factory defaults. In router mode browse to http://192.168.11.1 (bridge/AP mode: http://192.168.11.100), enter username 'admin' and password 'password' at the login prompt, click Log In, and step through the setup wizard.
routers.source_name: Buffalo — AirStation User Manual (PDF, manual.buffalo.jp)

routers.credential_note: CenturyLink prints a unique Admin Username and Admin Password on each C4000's sticker — there is no universal default. If the sticker is lost the preset credentials can't be recovered, only reset back to those on the label.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser to http://192.168.0.1 to reach the modem GUI. Sign in with the Admin Username and Admin Password printed on the sticker on the side/back/bottom of the C4000. These are unique per modem and cannot be retrieved if lost. To factory reset, press and hold the recessed Reset button ~10-15 seconds until the modem reboots, then sign in with the sticker's default Admin credentials.
routers.source_name: CenturyLink — Administrator Password, Advanced Modem Setup

routers.credential_note: No web admin password. Setup and management are done entirely through the Meraki Go mobile app and cloud account. The local status page is unlocked by the device serial number, not an admin/admin login.
routers.reset_steps: The Meraki Go GR12 is cloud-managed: download the Meraki Go app, create an account, and add the AP by scanning it — all admin control lives in the app/cloud, not a password on the device. A limited local page exists at http://my.meraki.com (or http://10.128.128.128) where the 'username' is the device serial number with no password, used only for uplink/static-IP settings. To factory reset, hold the Reset button until the AP reboots.
routers.source_name: Cisco Meraki Documentation (Meraki Go GR12 Installation Guide)

routers.credential_note: Wi-Fi 6 mesh-capable router with a dedicated EasyMesh pairing button, 4 antennas, WAN + 3x LAN ports, dual-band 2.4G/5G. No default admin password — the official quick installation guide confirms the setup wizard forces password creation on first login.
routers.reset_steps: With the device powered on, press the RESET button next to the LAN port for about 7 seconds until reset succeeds; on first login after reset the device goes straight to the setup wizard, which requires creating a password (used as both the Wi-Fi and router-admin password).
routers.source_name: COMFAST (Shenzhen Four Seas Global Link Network Technology) — CF-WR627AX Quick Installation Guide (official)

routers.credential_note: Plug-in Wi-Fi range extender/repeater (not a full router), single LAN/WAN port, dual-band 2.4G/5G, 4 operating modes (repeater/bridge/AP/router). Official quick installation guide confirms a genuine static default password 'admin' to enter setup, immediately followed by a mandatory password-set step.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the WPS/RESET button for about 6 seconds until the WiFi LED (which blinks once per second) turns off and stops blinking; release to restore factory defaults.
routers.source_name: COMFAST (Shenzhen Four Seas Global Link Network Technology) — Wireless Extender/Repeater Quick Installation Guide (official)

routers.credential_note: Cox provisions and manages Panoramic gateways primarily through the Panoramic Wifi app and your Cox account, not a shared web password. Local admin is 'admin' with a password on the label or one you set; there is no reliable universal admin/password on current firmware.
routers.reset_steps: Cox recommends managing the gateway through the Panoramic Wifi app (or online at cox.com after signing in with your Cox User ID). For local access, browse to http://192.168.0.1 and sign in with username 'admin'. If you have never changed it, try the password printed on the gateway label. To factory reset, press and hold the recessed Reset button (behind the gateway, above the phone ports) for a full 60 seconds — a shorter press only triggers WPS — then reconfigure via the app.
routers.source_name: Cox Residential Support — Setting up WiFi with the Panoramic WiFi Gateway

routers.credential_note: Cudy's login page at cudy.net / 192.168.10.1 prompts you to set a password on first access. Some units pre-fill 'admin' as the initial password, but current firmware has you create your own - there is no guaranteed admin/admin.
routers.reset_steps: Reset: with the router powered on, press and hold the RESET button for 10-15 seconds until the LEDs blink, then release and wait for reboot. Browse to http://cudy.net or 192.168.10.1 and set a new admin password.
routers.source_name: Cudy Official FAQ - How to log into the web interface of Cudy Router

routers.credential_note: D-Link's official support states the default for its ADSL modem/router (DSL series) is admin / admin at 192.168.1.1 — many older Airtel/BSNL/MTNL DSL units are these. D-Link also notes that units purchased after 2017 are secure by default with a unique password printed on the bottom of the unit, so check the label on newer hardware.
routers.reset_steps: Connect to the modem/router by LAN or Wi-Fi, open http://192.168.1.1 in a browser, and sign in with username admin and password admin (D-Link's documented default for its DSL series). If the login is rejected, the password was likely changed — keep the username admin and enter your own password. To factory reset, hold the recessed RESET button for about 10 seconds until the unit reboots, then log back in with admin / admin and reconfigure.
routers.source_name: D-Link — Default username and password for my ADSL modem/router

routers.credential_note: D-Link's documented default is username admin with a blank password — there is no admin/admin. D-Link's official login FAQ confirms admin with password blank by default for this era of routers.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser to http://192.168.0.1, select admin as the User Name and leave the Password blank, then click Log In. To factory reset, with the router on, press and hold the recessed Reset button on the bottom for about 10 seconds until it reboots; the password returns to blank.
routers.source_name: D-Link Support FAQ — How do I log into my router

routers.credential_note: The official D-Link DIR-655 manual and Quick Install Guide state the default username is admin and the default password is blank (leave the field empty). No admin/admin exists for this model.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser to http://192.168.0.1, choose Admin from the user drop-down, leave the password field blank, and click Log In. To reset, press and hold the Reset button on the back for about 10 seconds until the router reboots; the password reverts to blank.
routers.source_name: D-Link DIR-655 Quick Install Guide (official PDF)

routers.credential_note: The official D-Link DIR-825 user manual documents username admin with the password left blank by default. Owners are expected to set a password on first configuration.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser to http://192.168.0.1, enter admin as the username, leave the password blank, and log in. Factory reset: hold the Reset button on the underside for about 10 seconds with the unit powered on until it restarts; the password returns to blank.
routers.source_name: D-Link DIR-825 User Manual (official PDF)

routers.credential_note: Ships with NO admin password — the setup wizard forces you to create one. Classic login username is admin.
routers.reset_steps: With the router on, insert a paperclip into the recessed Reset hole on the back and hold ~10 seconds, then release to restore factory defaults.
routers.source_name: D-Link DIR-882 official User Manual (v1.00)

routers.credential_note: No default password — the login screen has only an Admin Password field (no username). Leave blank if the setup wizard hasn't run; otherwise use the password you created.
routers.reset_steps: Insert a paperclip into the recessed Reset hole on the back and hold longer than 10 seconds, then release to restore defaults.
routers.source_name: D-Link DIR-X1560 official User Manual (v1.00)

routers.credential_note: Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) AX1800 dual-band mesh-capable router (EXO AX line) — a lower tier than the AX5400 DIR-X5460. Web or D-Link Wi-Fi app setup. D-Link's Quick Install Guide states a static default: "You will be asked for your Device/Admin Password. By default this password is 'password'."
routers.reset_steps: Use a paperclip to press and hold the recessed Reset button for longer than 10 seconds to restore default settings, then reconnect to the Wi-Fi on the Quick Installation Card and set up again.
routers.source_name: D-Link DIR-X1870 Quick Installation Guide v1.01 — official PDF

routers.credential_note: AX3200 dual-band mesh-capable Wi-Fi 6 EXO-series router with Gigabit WAN — a lower-tier sibling of the DIR-X4860. The first web login prompts only for a Device/Admin Password with the factory value "password" (no username). D-Link: "You will be asked for your Device/Admin Password. By default this password is 'password'."
routers.reset_steps: Power the router on, then use a paperclip to hold the recessed rear Reset button ~10 seconds and release to restore factory defaults; the Device/Admin password reverts to "password".
routers.source_name: D-Link DIR-X3260 REV A1 Quick Installation Guide v1.01 — official PDF

routers.credential_note: AX4800 dual-band mesh-capable Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) EXO-series router with Gigabit WAN (Ethernet). Genuine static default: the first web login asks only for a Device/Admin Password whose factory value is the word "password" (no username field). D-Link: "You will be asked for your Device/Admin Password. By default this password is 'password'."
routers.reset_steps: With the router powered on, use a paperclip to hold the recessed rear Reset button ~10 seconds, then release to restore factory defaults (the Device/Admin password returns to "password").
routers.source_name: D-Link DIR-X4860 REV A Quick Installation Guide v1.00 — official PDF

routers.credential_note: Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) AX5400 dual-band mesh-capable router with a dual-core CPU and detachable antennas. D-Link's Quick Install Guide states a genuine static default: "You will be asked for your Device/Admin Password. By default this password is 'password'." Some revisions' user manuals instead cite a label-printed password, so confidence is medium.
routers.reset_steps: Use a paperclip to press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back for longer than 10 seconds to restore the router to default settings.
routers.source_name: D-Link DIR-X5460 Quick Installation Guide v1.10 — official PDF

routers.credential_note: Distinct from the already-covered Speedport Smart / Smart 4 Plus tier — Telekom's premium hybrid-mesh router. No username field and no admin/admin — login uses a unique per-unit device password (Gerätepasswort) printed on the device label or Routerpass, at http://speedport.ip. Telekom's own help page: 'Bei den Speedport-Routern steht das voreingestellte Gerätepasswort auf der Rückseite oder Unterseite des Gerätes oder dem Routerpass abgedruckt.'
routers.reset_steps: Premium hybrid fixed-line router with LTE bonding, mesh-WLAN base station, up to 12 antennas including DECT, 9,700 Mbit/s Wi-Fi class. Reset via the recessed button on the device; credentials revert to the printed Gerätepasswort after reset.
routers.source_name: Telekom Hilfe — Persönliches Kennwort in Speedport eintragen (official)

routers.credential_note: No universal default. The Speedport Smart uses a device-specific Gerätepasswort printed on the type plate (Typenschild) on the router and in the supplied router pass — there is no login username, only that device password.
routers.reset_steps: To log in: connect to the router, browse to http://speedport.ip (or 192.168.2.1) and enter the device password (Gerätepasswort). In the delivery state this is the value printed on the type plate on the base/back of the Speedport (also in the included router pass). To factory reset: with the router on, press and hold the recessed Reset button for at least 7 seconds until the lights flash; the device password returns to the one on the type plate.
routers.source_name: Telekom Hilfe — Gerätepasswort und WLAN-Schlüssel (Speedport)

routers.credential_note: Telekom's Wi-Fi 6-era DSL/fibre gateway — an earlier tier than the Speedport Smart 4 Plus already covered. No username and no shared default: the factory Gerätepasswort is unique per unit and login is at speedport.ip (192.168.2.1). Telekom: "Im Auslieferungszustand entspricht das Gerätepasswort der Angabe auf dem Typenschild Ihres Speedport bzw. der Angabe im mitgelieferten Router-Pass."
routers.reset_steps: Enter http://speedport.ip or http://192.168.2.1 in a browser and log in with the device password (Gerätepasswort) printed on the unit's type label / Router-Pass. To reset, hold the recessed Reset button with a pin for at least 15 seconds until the factory device password is active again.
routers.source_name: Deutsche Telekom Speedport Smart 3 Bedienungsanleitung — official (telekom.de)

routers.credential_note: DSL/VDSL and fibre (Glasfaser) capable Telekom gateway with integrated telephony (ships with DSL-Kabel, Glasfaser-Kabel and Telefon-Adapter) and an on-device display. No username field and no admin/admin — login uses a UNIQUE per-unit device password (Gerätepasswort) on the Typenschild and Router-Pass, at http://speedport.ip/.
routers.reset_steps: Open http://speedport.ip/ and sign in with the Gerätepasswort printed on the device label (Typenschild) and in the supplied Router-Pass; set your own in the config UI. Use the Neustart/Reset button to return to factory settings.
routers.source_name: Telekom Bedienungsanleitung — Speedport Smart 4 Plus (telekom.de, official)

routers.credential_note: Powerline (500 Mbps HomePlug) plus Wi-Fi 5 add-on adapter, the current entry point of the Magic 1 WiFi line. Gets a DHCP IP with no fixed default address; discovered via devolo Cockpit/app rather than a hostname. Web interface may be protected by a unique password printed on the type label, per the official manual.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the recessed reset button on the adapter for about 10 seconds until the LEDs flash, or use 'Restore factory settings' in devolo Cockpit or the Home Network App.
routers.source_name: devolo Magic 1 WiFi mini — official user manual

routers.credential_note: Wall-plug Powerline (G.hn, up to 2400 Mbps) plus dual-band mesh Wi-Fi 5 adapter (802.11a/b/g/n/ac up to 1200 Mbps, 4 antennas, band steering/roaming), with a pass-through socket and 2x gigabit LAN; sold in devolo's 'Mesh WiFi 2' kits. The built-in web interface has NO default password — assigning a login password is mandatory on first login. No fixed default IP: reach the UI via devolo Cockpit or the Home Network App. The Wi-Fi key (separate from the admin login) is unique and printed on the housing label.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button (next to the network jacks) for longer than 10 seconds until the LED flashes white, then disconnect from mains — this restores factory defaults (all settings lost).
routers.source_name: devolo — Manual devolo Magic 2 WiFi next (official PDF)

routers.credential_note: Gigabit Ethernet WAN broadband router with no built-in DSL modem — sits behind a separate modem/ONT, DrayTek's entry-level multi-WAN model. Genuine static default admin/admin confirmed in the official quick-start guide.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the recessed Factory Reset button on the rear panel for about 10 seconds until the ACT LED starts blinking, then release; the router reboots to factory defaults. Browse to http://192.168.1.1 and log in with admin/admin.
routers.source_name: DrayTek Vigor2135 Series Quick Start Guide v1.1 (official)

routers.credential_note: Wired-only VDSL2/ADSL2+ 35b-chipset security router with no built-in Wi-Fi — the base SKU in the Vigor2765 family (the RF/Vac variant adds 802.11ac and VoIP). Genuine static default admin/admin confirmed in the official quick-start guide.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the recessed Factory Reset button on the rear panel for about 10 seconds until the ACT LED starts blinking, then release; the router reboots to factory defaults. Browse to http://192.168.1.1 and log in with admin/admin.
routers.source_name: DrayTek Vigor2765 35b Series Quick Start Guide v1.8 (official)

routers.credential_note: VDSL2/ADSL2+ (35b) security firewall router with an integrated DSL modem and, on the RF model, 802.11ac Wi-Fi. Genuine static default admin/admin out of the box; the quick-start guide confirms you set a new password on first login, but admin/admin is the factory credential.
routers.reset_steps: With the router powered on (ACT LED blinking), press and hold the recessed Factory Reset hole for more than 5 seconds; when the ACT LED blinks rapidly, release to restart at defaults. Then browse to http://192.168.1.1 and log in.
routers.source_name: DrayTek Vigor2865 Quick Start Guide (official)

routers.credential_note: Dual-WAN Gigabit business security/VPN router — Ethernet WAN only (no DSL modem); the wired SKU has no Wi-Fi (the RF variant adds Wi-Fi 5). DrayTek ships a genuine static default of admin/admin; recent firmware then prompts you to set a new password, but admin/admin is the factory credential you first enter.
routers.reset_steps: With the router powered on (ACT LED blinking), press and hold the recessed Factory Reset hole for more than 5 seconds; when the ACT LED blinks rapidly, release and let it restart at factory defaults. Then browse to http://192.168.1.1 and log in.
routers.source_name: DrayTek Vigor2927 Quick Start Guide (official)

routers.credential_note: SMB multi-WAN (4x GbE WAN) security router/firewall built for VPN concentration and load-balancing at the edge — no built-in Wi-Fi or DSL modem, DrayTek's business-tier model above the Vigor2927. Genuine static default admin/admin confirmed in the official quick-start guide.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the recessed Factory Reset button on the rear panel for about 10 seconds until the ACT LED starts blinking, then release; the router reboots to factory defaults. Browse to http://192.168.1.1 and log in with admin/admin (the system then prompts a password change).
routers.source_name: DrayTek Vigor3910 Series Quick Start Guide v1.7 (official)

routers.credential_note: 802.11ac business access point (PoE, wall/ceiling mount) — DrayTek's AP line, a distinct default-IP scheme (.1.2) from the Vigor router family (.1.1) already covered. Official Quick Start Guide: 'Please enter "admin/admin" as the Username/Password and click Login.'
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Factory Reset button for about 10 seconds until the LEDs flash, then release to restore factory defaults. Browse to http://192.168.1.2 (or http://vigorap.com over Wi-Fi) and log in with admin/admin.
routers.source_name: DrayTek VigorAP 903 802.11ac Access Point Quick Start Guide V2.1 (official)

routers.credential_note: N300 (802.11b/g/n, 2.4GHz-only, up to 300 Mbps) entry-level Wi-Fi 4 router/AP/range-extender combo. Wired login at http://192.168.2.1; the official User Manual's Login section and the product-label default table both state a genuine static default of admin / 1234 (a later FAQ line inconsistently prints admin/admin — the label value governs).
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the WPS/Reset button on the back panel for at least 10 seconds until the power LED begins to flash, then release and wait for the router to restart; defaults return to admin / 1234 at http://192.168.2.1.
routers.source_name: Edimax BR-6428nS V5 User Manual (v1.3, 08-2021) — download.edimax.com (official)

routers.credential_note: There is no admin/admin default. Each EE Smart Hub has a unique admin password printed on the card on the back of the hub, separate from the WiFi password.
routers.reset_steps: To log in: connect to the hub, browse to 192.168.1.254 and enter the admin password printed on the card on the back of the hub (this is different from the WiFi password, which is on the same card). To factory reset: with the hub on, press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back for about 20 seconds until it restarts; the network name, WiFi password and admin password revert to the values on the back card.
routers.source_name: EE Broadband Help — Change the WiFi and admin password on your Hub

routers.credential_note: EE's fibre gateway line (Smart Hub Plus / 6 Plus / 7 Plus) — distinct from the older EE Smart Hub already covered. The Hub Manager admin password is separate from the Wi-Fi password and is printed per-unit on the card on the back; login is at 192.168.1.254 with no username. EE: "That password is also on the card on the back of the hub."
routers.reset_steps: Type 192.168.1.254 in the browser address bar and press Enter, then log in with the admin password printed on the card on the back of the hub. A factory reset restores that printed admin password.
routers.source_name: EE Broadband Help — Change the WiFi Password and Admin Password on Your Hub (official)

routers.credential_note: App-only. There is no admin web page and no admin/admin default password. The only password is the Wi-Fi password you create in the eero app.
routers.reset_steps: eero 6+ is managed only in the eero app. To hard reset: with the eero powered on, hold the reset button on the back until the LED flashes red (~15 seconds), then release; when it blinks blue it is ready to set up. Re-add it in the app and set your Wi-Fi credentials.
routers.source_name: eero Help Center

routers.credential_note: App-only mesh. No web interface and no factory admin/admin. All configuration, including the Wi-Fi password you pick, lives in the eero app under your Amazon/eero account.
routers.reset_steps: There is no browser login for eero — use the eero app. To hard reset: powered on, hold the reset button until the LED flashes red (about 15 seconds), release, and wait for the blue blink. Add the eero back in the app and choose a new Wi-Fi name and password.
routers.source_name: eero Help Center

routers.credential_note: App-only — there is no admin web page and no admin/admin default. You create and change the Wi-Fi password in the eero app under Settings > Wifi name & password. There are no separate router login credentials.
routers.reset_steps: eero has no web admin page — everything is managed in the eero mobile app. To factory (hard) reset: with the eero powered on, press and hold the reset button on the back until the LED flashes red (about 15 seconds), then release. When the light blinks blue the unit is ready. Reopen the eero app (signed into your Amazon/eero account) and add the eero back to your network; you set the Wi-Fi name and password there.
routers.source_name: eero Help Center

routers.credential_note: App-only. No web admin, no default admin/admin. The Wi-Fi password is one you set in the eero app during setup; view or change it under Settings > Wifi name & password.
routers.reset_steps: eero is administered only through the eero mobile app. To hard reset: with the unit powered on, hold the reset button on the back until the LED flashes red (~15 seconds), then release. Wait for the light to blink blue, then re-add the eero in the app and set your Wi-Fi name and password.
routers.source_name: eero Help Center

routers.credential_note: EnGenius documents a static default of admin / admin at 192.168.1.1 for standalone-mode devices and the local access page of cloud APs. Cloud-managed (EnGenius Cloud app) is the primary path for ECW models; the local admin/admin login is for direct setup.
routers.reset_steps: For a standalone EnGenius access point, connect a computer to the AP and browse to http://192.168.1.1 (or http://EnGenius.local). If the AP can't find a DHCP server it falls back to 192.168.1.1. Log in with username 'admin' and password 'admin', then change the password. To factory reset, hold the AP's Reset button for about 10 seconds until it reboots, restoring admin/admin.
routers.source_name: Doctor EnGenius Help Center (default IP, username and password)

routers.credential_note: Etisalat's official configuration manual documents http://192.168.2.1 with admin / admin for this e-Life router. This applies to the legacy Aztech HW550-3G; current e& fibre service ships different ONTs whose admin password is typically printed on the device label rather than a universal admin/admin.
routers.reset_steps: Connect to the router by LAN or Wi-Fi, open http://192.168.2.1 in a browser, and sign in with username admin and password admin (Etisalat's documented default for this unit). Complete Internet setup with the PPPoE credentials from your e-Life card. To factory reset, hold the recessed RESET button for about 10 seconds until the unit reboots, then log back in at 192.168.2.1 and set a new admin password under System > Password.
routers.source_name: Etisalat UAE — Aztech HW550-3G Configuration Manual

routers.credential_note: Compact home/small-office firewall/router gateway — the higher-throughput sibling of the base Firewalla Blue, and the first Blue-line SKU in this seed (only Gold and Purple were covered previously). Managed entirely from the Firewalla app; Firewalla's own help center: 'the Web interface is a complementary management interface to the mobile app and is supported on all Firewalla devices Blue and up' — no device login exists.
routers.reset_steps: Pairing and factory reset are handled entirely through the Firewalla app; there is no on-box web-admin credential to reset.
routers.source_name: Firewalla Help Center — Web Interfaces for Firewalla (official)

routers.credential_note: Multi-gigabit firewall/router security gateway (Gold Original/Rev B/Plus: 4x 1G routable ports; Gold SE adds 2.5G; Gold Pro adds 10G/2.5G). Managed entirely from the Firewalla iOS/Android app — there is NO web-admin username/password on the box. Setup: install the app, tap +, and pair using the bundled red security dongle. The optional web interface (my.firewalla.com) authenticates through the paired app, not device credentials.
routers.reset_steps: Setup/pairing and factory reset are driven from the Firewalla app; the hardware reset varies by model (Gold Pro has a dedicated Reset button, others reset via SD-card reflash) — see Firewalla's 'How to reset Firewalla box' article.
routers.source_name: Firewalla Help Center — Firewalla Gold Series Installation Guide

routers.credential_note: Gigabit firewall/router security gateway with dual-band Wi-Fi. Managed entirely from the Firewalla iOS/Android app — there is NO on-box web login. Setup and pairing are done in the app; the complementary web interface (my.firewalla.com), supported on Firewalla Blue and up, authenticates via the paired mobile app rather than device credentials.
routers.reset_steps: Pairing and factory reset are handled through the Firewalla app; see Firewalla's 'How to reset Firewalla box' article for the hardware reset procedure.
routers.source_name: Firewalla Help Center — Web Interfaces for Firewalla

routers.credential_note: Fibre/xDSL gateway (Freebox Server) with integrated telephony, managed via Freebox OS. No factory admin/admin: on first connection the user creates their own administrator password, gated by a physical confirmation on the Freebox Server itself. Login is by that user-set password at mafreebox.freebox.fr.
routers.reset_steps: From a device connected to the Freebox, go to http://mafreebox.freebox.fr/ and click Première connexion, then define your own administrator password (physical confirmation on the Freebox Server is required). If lost, use J'ai perdu mon mot de passe, which also requires physical validation on the box.
routers.source_name: Assistance Free — Freebox OS : accéder à Freebox OS depuis mon domicile (official)

routers.credential_note: Frontier routers (Arris/Sagemcom FiberOptic gateways) print the admin password on the device label — it varies by unit and model, so there is no single universal default. Older Frontier DSL units used admin/password, but fiber gateways rely on the label value.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser to http://192.168.1.1 (some models use 192.168.254.254). The Admin Username is usually 'admin' and the Admin Password is printed on the label on the side/bottom of the router. To factory reset, press and hold the recessed Reset button ~10-15 seconds until the router restarts, then sign in with the credentials on the label.
routers.source_name: Frontier Help Center — Change Your Wi-Fi Network Name and Password

routers.credential_note: Beryl AX (GL-MT3000) is GL.iNet's pocket travel router. No admin password is shipped with it — the first page at 192.168.8.1 asks you to create one. The wireless name and key on its label are unique to that unit, not a universal pair.
routers.reset_steps: Reset: with the router powered on, press and hold the RESET button for about 10 seconds until the LEDs flash, then release and wait for reboot. Rejoin the label's wireless network, open 192.168.8.1, pick a language, and create your admin password.
routers.source_name: GL.iNet Official Docs - Beryl AX (GL-MT3000) User Guide

routers.credential_note: Flint (GL-AX1800) is the desktop model in the range. It arrives without an admin password; your first visit to 192.168.8.1 requires you to make one, at least 5 characters. Its bottom label prints a per-device wireless name and key, which is a separate thing entirely.
routers.reset_steps: Reset: with power on, keep RESET depressed near 10 seconds until the LEDs flash, then let go and allow the reboot. Reconnect over the wireless network from the bottom label, go to 192.168.8.1, choose a language, and enter an admin password of your own.
routers.source_name: GL.iNet Official Docs - Flint (GL-AX1800) User Guide

routers.credential_note: The Flint 2 is GL.iNet's AX6000 WiFi 6 router with 2.5 Gbps WAN/LAN ports. Official docs state the admin panel has no default password — you create your own (minimum 5 characters) at first login on 192.168.8.1. Login is password-only with no username, separate from the Wi-Fi key.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the physical RESET button about 10 seconds until the LED flashes to restore factory defaults, then browse to 192.168.8.1 and set a new admin password.
routers.source_name: GL.iNet official router docs (GL-MT6000)

routers.credential_note: Slate AX (GL-AXT1800) is the AX1800-class travel unit. Nothing is preset on it: 192.168.8.1 opens a create-password step before any settings appear. The SSID and key on the bottom sticker differ per device and are not the admin credential.
routers.reset_steps: Reset: hold RESET for roughly 10 seconds while the unit is powered, release once the LEDs flash, and let it restart. Attach to the sticker's wireless network, load 192.168.8.1, select a language, and define the admin password you want.
routers.source_name: GL.iNet Official Docs - Slate AX (GL-AXT1800) User Guide

routers.credential_note: App-only: setup and management are entirely through the Google Home app. There is NO web admin page, NO default IP login, and NO default username/password.
routers.reset_steps: Factory reset via the Google Home app (Wi-Fi › Settings › Factory reset network), or hold the factory-reset button on the point until the light pulses.
routers.source_name: Google Nest Help — Set up Nest Wifi

routers.credential_note: App-only via the Google Home app. There is no admin/admin default; you create the network name and password during setup. Nest Wifi Pro cannot be mixed in a mesh with older Nest Wifi or Google Wifi points.
routers.reset_steps: Nest Wifi Pro has no web admin — it is set up and managed in the Google Home app. To factory reset the router: press and hold the factory reset button on the bottom for about 10 seconds; the light flashes yellow, then turns solid yellow — release the button. The reset can take up to 10 minutes; do not unplug during it. Then open the Google Home app and set the device up again (you pick a new network name and password).
routers.source_name: Google Nest Help

routers.credential_note: Dual-band 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5) gigabit VPN router (GWN7052; GWN7052F is the SFP/fibre variant) — 1x gigabit WAN plus gigabit LAN, standalone or GWN.Cloud managed. The default admin password is UNIQUE per unit and printed on the MAC tag — not a static admin/admin — and a password change is forced at first boot.
routers.reset_steps: Browse to https://192.168.80.1 and log in with admin plus the default password printed on the MAC/label sticker on the unit; at first boot or after a factory reset you are required to set new admin and user passwords before the web UI loads.
routers.source_name: Grandstream GWN7062 & GWN7052/F User Manual — documentation.grandstream.com (official)

routers.credential_note: Dual-band Wi-Fi 6 VPN/security router in the GWN70x2 line — a distinct, higher-throughput model from the GWN7052 already covered, sharing the same default IP scheme. Official documentation: 'the default administrator's username is "admin" and the default password is printed on the MAC tag of the unit' — forced change on first boot or after a factory reset.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the reset button for about 10 seconds until the unit reboots to factory defaults, then browse to https://192.168.80.1 and log in with 'admin' plus the unique password printed on the MAC tag of the unit.
routers.source_name: Grandstream GWN7062 & GWN7052/F User Manual — documentation.grandstream.com (official)

routers.credential_note: 802.11ax 2x2 Wi-Fi 6 ceiling/wall access point in the GWN76xx line, DHCP/discovery-based rather than a fixed static IP — distinct form factor from the GWN70x2 routers. Official Quick Installation Guide: 'The default administrator username is "admin" and the default random password can be found at the sticker on the GWN7660.'
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the reset button until the unit reboots to factory defaults. Discover it via the GWN Discovery Tool or https://gwn_<MAC-address>.local/, then log in with 'admin' plus the random password printed on the unit's sticker.
routers.source_name: Grandstream GWN7660 Quick Installation Guide — documentation.grandstream.com (official)

routers.credential_note: Enterprise 802.11ax Wi-Fi 6 AP — dual-band 4x4:4 MU-MIMO, DL/UL OFDMA, up to 512 clients, 2.5G + 1G PoE/PoE+. In standalone mode, reach it at https://gwn_<mac>.local; the username is admin with a UNIQUE random default password on the device sticker (not a shared static default). Grandstream: "The default administrator username is 'admin' and the default random password can be found on the sticker on the GWN7664."
routers.reset_steps: Hold the physical Reset button ~7 seconds until the LEDs flash to restore factory defaults; the per-device random default password on the sticker then applies again.
routers.source_name: Grandstream GWN7664 Quick Installation Guide (official)

routers.credential_note: No universal default — the management password is set on first setup (or printed on the nameplate for WPS-initiated setup).
routers.reset_steps: With a pin, hold the recessed RESET button until the indicator light goes out/blinks, then wait for the router to restart to factory defaults.
routers.source_name: Huawei official support (router web management login)

routers.credential_note: No universal default — set on first setup; default gateway 192.168.3.1.
routers.reset_steps: With a pin, hold the recessed RESET button until the indicator light goes out/blinks, then wait for the router to restart to factory defaults.
routers.source_name: Huawei WiFi WS5200 official support page

routers.credential_note: iiNet's Technicolor TG-789vac v2 VDSL2/ADSL2+ gateway (802.11ac dual-band, built-in VoIP phone ports). Username is admin; the admin password is UNIQUE per unit, printed under 'GUI Login' on the barcode sticker — the sample values in iiNet's guide are not a shared default.
routers.reset_steps: Browse to http://10.1.1.1 and log in with username admin and the default password shown under 'GUI Login' on the modem's barcode sticker. To reset, hold the recessed reset button about 10 seconds until the modem restarts, then log in again with the sticker password.
routers.source_name: iiNet TG789 Broadband Gateway Quick Setup Guide (help.iinet.net.au, official)

routers.credential_note: Jio's official support does not publish any web admin username/password — JioFiber is administered entirely through the MyJio / JioHome mobile apps. Any 'admin/admin' login shown on aggregator sites does not reflect how Jio documents managing the unit.
routers.reset_steps: JioFiber is managed from the MyJio app, not a web admin page. Open MyJio, sign in with your JioFiber number, choose your Fiber account, and change the Wi-Fi name/password under the device / Wi-Fi settings (JioAirFiber uses the JioHome app with mobile number + OTP). To hard reset the ONT, hold the recessed RESET pinhole on the back for about 10 seconds until it reboots, then reconfigure Wi-Fi from the app. There is no admin/admin web login to sign into.
routers.source_name: Jio Help — Change JioFiber Router (Wi-Fi/SSID) password

routers.credential_note: AX1800 dual-band Wi-Fi 6 mesh router; 5x 1GbE ports (4x RJ-45 + 1 combo RJ-45/SFP), USB 2.0 + USB 3.0. Sold as 'Giga' (KN-1011) in the EAEU/CIS market and as 'Hero' globally — identical hardware. No factory-default admin password: the web setup wizard forces you to set the 'admin' account password on first run.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button ~10-12 seconds until the status LED starts flashing, then release to restore factory defaults. Reconnect, open my.keenetic.net (or 192.168.1.1), and the Initial Setup Wizard requires you to create the admin password before proceeding.
routers.source_name: Keenetic Support (support.keenetic.com)

routers.credential_note: AX3000 dual-band Wi-Fi 6 gigabit mesh router (574 Mbps 2.4GHz + 2402 Mbps 5GHz), 4x 1GbE ports, USB 3.0, with MU-MIMO, beamforming and OFDMA. No factory-default admin password: the setup wizard forces creation of the 'admin' account password on first run.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button ~10-12 seconds until the status LED starts flashing, then release to restore factory defaults. Reconnect and open my.keenetic.net (or 192.168.1.1); the Initial Setup Wizard requires you to create the admin password before continuing.
routers.source_name: Keenetic Support (support.keenetic.com)

routers.credential_note: 9x GbE + 1x SFP mesh Wi-Fi 5 (AC2600) router with USB 2.0/3.0 ports, dual-core MediaTek CPU — Keenetic's previous-generation flagship before the Wi-Fi 7 Titan line. No factory-default admin password: the setup wizard forces creation of the 'admin' account password on first run.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the recessed Reset button with a paperclip for about 10-12 seconds until the Status LED begins flashing rapidly, then release; this clears the admin password and all settings and restarts the Initial Setup Wizard.
routers.source_name: Keenetic Support — Peak (KN-2710): What login and password do I need to enter in the app?

routers.credential_note: Wi-Fi 7 (BE7200) mesh multi-gigabit router with USB 3.2/2.0 ports — Keenetic's current flagship, successor to the Peak/Ultra AC2600 line. No factory-default admin password: the setup wizard forces creation of the 'admin' account password on first run.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the recessed Reset button with a paperclip for about 10-12 seconds until the Status LED begins flashing rapidly, then release; this clears the admin password and all settings and restarts the Initial Setup Wizard.
routers.source_name: Keenetic Support — Titan (KN-1812): Web Interface

routers.credential_note: AC1300 dual-band Wi-Fi 5 mesh router; 5x Gigabit Ethernet ports and two USB ports. Sold as 'Viva' (KN-1912) in the EAEU/CIS market and as 'Skipper' globally — identical hardware. No factory-default admin password: the setup wizard forces creation of the 'admin' account password on first run.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button ~10-12 seconds until the status LED starts flashing, then release to restore factory defaults. Reconnect and open my.keenetic.net (or 192.168.1.1); the Initial Setup Wizard requires you to create the admin password before continuing.
routers.source_name: Keenetic Support (support.keenetic.com)

routers.credential_note: VDSL/bonded-VDSL/fiber wireless gateway family (OEM: Actiontec) issued by Kinetic by Windstream — note the unusual 192.168.254.254 admin address. Username is admin; the password is unique per unit on the side sticker. Windstream: "Password: The password is located on a sticker on the side of the modem ... different on every single T3200/T3260/T3280/T4220 modem."
routers.reset_steps: Factory-reset via the reset button on the modem; after reset, log in at http://192.168.254.254 with the admin password printed on the side-label sticker (unique per unit).
routers.source_name: Kinetic by Windstream — official support FAQ (Actiontec T3200/T3260/T3280/T4220)

routers.credential_note: VDSL/ADSL dual-band wireless gateway (OEM: Zyxel) issued by Kinetic by Windstream. Username is admin; the admin password is unique to each unit and printed on the bottom sticker — not a shared default. Windstream: "The customer can enter the Administrator Password which is located on the sticker on the bottom of the modem. This password is different on every single VMG4927."
routers.reset_steps: Factory-reset via the recessed reset button on the device; after reset, log in with the Administrator Password on the bottom-label sticker (unique per unit).
routers.source_name: Kinetic by Windstream — official support FAQ (Zyxel VMG4927-B50A)

routers.credential_note: No admin/admin: the documented default password is 'admin' with no username. The E5600 uses a plain http:// connection (unlike the HTTPS-only E7350/E8450). You should set your own password at first login.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button on the bottom for about 10 seconds until the lights flash, then release to restore factory defaults. Browse to http://myrouter.local (or http://192.168.1.1, or http://192.168.11.1 if connected behind an existing network) and log in with the default password 'admin'.
routers.source_name: Linksys Official Support — Log in to the Dual-Band WiFi Router's web interface

routers.credential_note: No admin/admin: the default web-UI password is 'admin' with no username field. Newer firmware forces an HTTPS connection, so an http:// address will not load the login page.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button on the bottom for about 10 seconds until the lights flash, then release to restore factory defaults.
