Current firmware requires HTTPS: browse to https://myrouter.local (or https://192.168.1.1, or https://192.168.10.1 if it is behind an upstream connection) and log in with the default password 'admin'.
routers.source_name: Linksys Official Support — Log in to the Dual-Band WiFi Router's web interface

routers.credential_note: No admin/admin: the router's default web-interface password is 'admin' with no username. Latest firmware forces HTTPS, so use https:// (an http:// URL will fail). You are expected to set your own password on first login.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button on the bottom for about 10 seconds until the lights flash, then release and let it reboot to factory defaults. On current firmware an HTTPS connection is required: browse to https://myrouter.local (or https://192.168.1.1, or https://10.0.0.1 if the router sits behind another gateway) and log in with the default password 'admin'.
routers.source_name: Linksys Official Support — Log in to the Dual-Band WiFi Router's web interface

routers.credential_note: AX5400 dual-band Wi-Fi 6 standalone router (non-mesh) that uses a non-standard default LAN IP (192.168.79.1) rather than the common 192.168.1.1 — distinct from the Velop mesh SKUs already covered. Linksys's own FAQ: the default IP is 192.168.79.1, and admin is the default username and password.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the reset button at the back of the router for 10 seconds, then release — the power light turns off and starts blinking blue as it restores factory defaults.
routers.source_name: Linksys Support — Linksys E9450 FAQs (official)

routers.credential_note: Official Linksys default is admin. The Smart Wi-Fi setup wizard prompts you to change it; a Recovery Key on the label is used for recovery.
routers.reset_steps: With a pin, hold the Reset button 10 seconds until the light blinks, then release (or power-cycle for 30 seconds).
routers.source_name: Linksys official Support Article 378

routers.credential_note: No admin/admin: Linksys documents the default administrative password of an unconfigured router as 'admin' with no username. The label's unique password is the WiFi key, not the admin login. Setup normally forces you to create your own admin password.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button for 11 seconds; watch for three slow red pulses and release the button on the fourth red pulse — the router reboots to factory defaults. Reconnect to the default WiFi (LinksysSetupXXX, unique WiFi password on the node's label) and set it up in the Linksys app, or log in at http://192.168.1.1 with the admin password. (Software reset: web UI > Router Settings > Troubleshooting > Diagnostics > Factory reset.)
routers.source_name: Linksys Official Support — Hydra Pro 6E, MR7500 FAQs

routers.credential_note: MAX-STREAM AC3000 tri-band Wi-Fi 5 mesh-capable router. App-driven setup creates a secure admin password automatically — there is no static default; a Recovery Key on the label is used for recovery. Web access via myrouter.local or https://192.168.1.1. Linksys: "We created a secure admin password during setup."
routers.reset_steps: Change the admin password in Linksys app > Router Administration > Change Router Password. Full factory reset: hold the Reset button until the top light blinks red, releasing when it turns bright red.
routers.source_name: Linksys MR9000 User Guide — official PDF

routers.credential_note: There is no admin/admin here: the documented default administrator password of an unconfigured MR7350 is literally 'admin' (no username). The unique password printed on the bottom label is the WiFi password, not the admin password. Linksys prompts you to set your own admin password during app setup.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button on the bottom of the router for about 10 seconds until the lights indicate a reset, then release and let it reboot to factory defaults. Reconnect to the default WiFi (_LinksysSetupXXX, using the unique WiFi password on the bottom label) or plug in by Ethernet, then finish setup in the Linksys app, or log in at http://192.168.1.1 with the admin password. If you forgot a changed password, use the 5-digit recovery code on the product label.
routers.source_name: Linksys Official Support — MR7350 FAQs

routers.credential_note: App-first setup (Linksys app). No universal web default — the admin password is created during setup; a Recovery Key printed on the device label is used for recovery. Login is password-only (no username).
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button on the bottom of the node ~10 seconds until the light turns red, then release to restore factory defaults.
routers.source_name: Linksys official Support Article 107

routers.credential_note: Velop Pro 6E tri-band Wi-Fi 6E Cognitive Mesh node. App-driven setup via the Linksys app — there is NO preset default admin password; the app auto-generates one, and recovery uses the Recovery Key on the label. Web access via myrouter.local or https://192.168.1.1. Linksys: "the app will automatically generate a password to secure your node."
routers.reset_steps: Recovery uses the Reset Password / Recovery Key printed on the node's product label. Full factory reset: hold the Reset button on the bottom of the node until the light blinks red.
routers.source_name: Linksys MX6200 Velop Pro 6E FAQs (official support)

routers.credential_note: Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) tri-band BE11000 mesh system — a Wi-Fi 7 tier above the AC-class Velop MX already covered. App-first setup via the Linksys app; each node ships with a unique Wi-Fi password and Recovery Key on its underside label. Linksys: "The default administrative password automatically changes to an unknown password if the router has been set up with the Linksys app."
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button on the bottom of the node until the light turns red, then set up again via the Linksys app. If the admin password is unknown, use the Recovery Key on the node's label to customize a new one.
routers.source_name: Linksys Support Article 335 — MBE7000 Velop Pro 7 FAQs (official)

routers.credential_note: Local admin default is admin per official docs; the setup wizard prompts changing it and a Recovery Key on the label is used for recovery.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button 10 seconds until the power LED flashes to restore factory settings.
routers.source_name: Linksys official WRT3200ACM User Guide

routers.credential_note: The official Linksys user guide documents a genuine universal default: leave the username blank and use admin as the password. This is one of the few classic models with a true factory default (not admin/admin) — Linksys recommends changing it immediately from Administration > Management.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser and go to http://192.168.1.1. When the login box appears, leave the User Name blank and enter admin as the password (lowercase). To factory reset, press and hold the Reset button on the back with a paperclip for about 15 seconds until the front lights flash, then release and wait for the router to reboot; the login returns to blank username / admin password.
routers.source_name: Linksys WRT54G User Guide (official PDF)

routers.credential_note: Halo mesh is set up via the MERCUSYS app; the web page at mwlogin.net signs in with the MERCUSYS ID / password you created during app setup. There is no admin/admin default.
routers.reset_steps: Reset a Halo unit: press and hold its RESET button for about 10 seconds until the LED changes, then release and wait for reboot. Reconfigure through the MERCUSYS app; the web page (mwlogin.net or LAN IP 192.168.68.1) signs in with the app credentials you created.
routers.source_name: Mercusys Official - How to log in to the web management page of Halo

routers.credential_note: AX1800 mesh configured through the MERCUSYS app with a Mercusys ID — no generic default login. The web page at mwlogin.net signs in with that Mercusys ID password. Gateway 192.168.1.1 is Mercusys's standard default (not model-confirmed).
routers.reset_steps: Reset from within the MERCUSYS app, or hold the Reset button on a Halo unit until the LED changes, then re-run setup in the app.
routers.source_name: MERCUSYS official FAQ 252 (Halo web login)

routers.credential_note: No default password. On first access to mwlogin.net the router forces you to create an admin password - there is no admin/admin. (Some older Mercusys models accepted admin/admin, but current firmware does not.)
routers.reset_steps: Reset: with the router powered on, use a pin to press and hold the RESET button on the rear panel for about 10 seconds until it reboots, then release. Browse to http://mwlogin.net (click Advanced to accept the self-signed-certificate warning) and create a new admin password.
routers.source_name: Mercusys Official - How to Log in to the Web Management Page

routers.credential_note: Label-based — the default network name and password used to connect during setup are printed on the bottom of the main M3 pod. Setup and management are done in the My Mesh app; you set your own network password there. There is no admin/admin default.
routers.reset_steps: Meshforce M3 is set up with the My Mesh app (download it before starting). The default Wi-Fi name and password used to join the main unit during setup are printed on the bottom label of the primary pod. To factory reset, press and hold the reset button on the unit with a pin until the LED indicator blinks, then release and set the system up again in the My Mesh app.
routers.source_name: Meshforce M3 Setup Guide

routers.credential_note: 5G (SA/NSA) CPE router on RouterOS — quad-core ARM64, 4x GbE + 1x 2.5G, USB-A, micro-SIM. RouterOS default is user admin with NO password on units without a per-device label (some units instead print user/wireless passwords on the sticker). MikroTik: "The username is 'admin,' and there is no password (or, for some models, check user and wireless passwords on the sticker)."
routers.reset_steps: Power off, hold the reset button while powering on, and keep holding until the LED starts flashing, then release to reset RouterOS configuration to defaults.
routers.source_name: MikroTik Documentation — Quick Guide: Chateau 5G ax (official)

routers.credential_note: LTE Category 12 CPE gateway with an integrated modem (LTE bands 1/3/5/7/8/20/28/38/40) and dual-band Wi-Fi 5 (2.4GHz b/g/n + 5GHz a/n/ac), RouterOS v7. Username is admin; newer units carry a unique password on the sticker (no static default), some ship blank and prompt set-on-first-login. Access WebFig/WinBox at 192.168.88.1.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button during boot until the green LED flashes, then release to reset the RouterOS configuration.
routers.source_name: MikroTik Documentation — Chateau LTE12 User Manual

routers.credential_note: The hAP ac2 is the 802.11ac generation of MikroTik's hAP line. RouterOS uses the account name admin, and on most units that account has no password at all out of the box. Some later production batches instead print a unique password on the case sticker, and RouterOS v7 refuses to continue until you pick one.
routers.reset_steps: Keep RESET pressed while the unit powers up, and let go once the green LED begins flashing. RouterOS drops back to its factory configuration.
routers.source_name: MikroTik official documentation — hAP ac² manual

routers.credential_note: 802.11ax hardware: the hAP ax2 is the WiFi 6 member of the same family, reached at 192.168.88.1. The login name stays admin. A blank password is the shipped state for most stock, but check the case sticker first, because newer batches carry a unique one printed there. RouterOS v7 will make you choose a password during that initial session.
routers.reset_steps: Power on with RESET held down, releasing the moment the green LED starts to flash. That wipes the RouterOS configuration back to defaults.
routers.source_name: MikroTik official documentation — hAP ax² manual

routers.credential_note: Dual-band Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) home router on RouterOS v7 with gigabit Ethernet ports. Username is admin; the unique default password is retrieved from a pull-out card holder near the product information on the housing (no static default). Some units ship blank and prompt a password on first login. Access WebFig/WinBox at 192.168.88.1.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button during power-up until the LED starts flashing (~5s), then release to reset the configuration.
routers.source_name: MikroTik Documentation — hAP ax3 User Manual

routers.credential_note: 5-port desktop Gigabit Ethernet router with no Wi-Fi, microSD slot, USB-A, 8-30V DC/passive PoE on Ether1 — MikroTik's compact wired-only home/small-office router. Username admin with no password on most stock (check the case sticker on some production batches) per the official MikroTik documentation.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the recessed RESET button while powering the unit on; release once the LED begins blinking to restore RouterOS factory defaults. If IP access is unavailable, connect via WinBox using the device's MAC address on the LAN side.
routers.source_name: MikroTik Documentation — hEX User Manual

routers.credential_note: 9-port cloud router: 8x Gigabit + 1x 2.5G SFP, USB 3.0, PoE-in on Ether1/PoE-out on Ether8, single-band 2.4GHz Wi-Fi 6 radio, RouterOS Level 5 — MikroTik's PoE-focused small-office router. Username admin with no password on most stock (check the case sticker on some batches) per the official MikroTik documentation.
routers.reset_steps: Power on the unit with RESET held down, letting go the moment the LED begins to blink to reset RouterOS to defaults. If IP access is unavailable, connect via WinBox using the device's MAC address on the LAN side.
routers.source_name: MikroTik Documentation — L009UiGS-2HaxD-IN User Manual

routers.credential_note: Wired-only RouterOS v7 desktop router: 7x 1G + 1x 2.5G Ethernet + 1x 10G SFP+, quad-core ARM 88F7040 @1.4GHz, 1GB RAM, USB 3.0, no Wi-Fi. Username is admin; current production ships a unique password printed on the packaging/label (no static default), while older stock ships blank and prompts you to set one on first login. Access WebFig/WinBox at 192.168.88.1.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button during power-up until the green LED starts flashing (~5s), then release to reset the RouterOS configuration to defaults.
routers.source_name: MikroTik Documentation — RB5009UG+S+IN User Manual

routers.credential_note: Weatherproof outdoor Wi-Fi 6 access point, dual-chain 2.4GHz + 5GHz radios, 2x Gigabit Ethernet with PoE-in on Ether1, IP54 rated — MikroTik's outdoor AP line. Username admin with no password on most stock (check the case sticker on some batches) per the official MikroTik documentation.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the RESET button on the underside while powering the unit on, releasing once the LED starts blinking to restore factory defaults. Connect via WinBox to the device's MAC address from the LAN side if IP access fails.
routers.source_name: MikroTik Documentation — wAP ax User Manual

routers.credential_note: Genuine documented factory default is admin / motorola (lowercase). The default is also printed on the bottom label. It is a modem, so this page shows connection status and settings, not Wi-Fi.
routers.reset_steps: The MB8611 is a DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem (no Wi-Fi). Open a browser to http://192.168.100.1 and log in with username 'admin' and password 'motorola' (all lowercase), then change the password. If you've forgotten a changed password, factory reset by inserting a paperclip into the recessed Reset hole on the back and holding about 10 seconds until the modem reboots, which restores admin/motorola.
routers.source_name: Motorola Home Networking Support (MB8611 admin login)

routers.credential_note: Username admin; the password is the UNIQUE value printed on the device's bottom label (entered lowercase) — there is no shared default password.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the recessed reset button on the rear ~10+ seconds until it restarts to restore factory defaults.
routers.source_name: Motorola MG8702 official User Manual

routers.credential_note: 1U desktop security gateway: dual-core Intel Atom C3338R, 2x 1GbE + 4x 2.5GbE flexible WAN/LAN ports, 4GB RAM, runs pfSense Plus, no Wi-Fi — the entry model above the SG-2100. Genuine static default admin/pfsense confirmed in the official initial-configuration docs; pfSense Plus 24.03+ forces a password change on first login.
routers.reset_steps: At the console/serial menu choose option 4 'Reset to factory defaults', or use Diagnostics > Factory Defaults in the pfSense GUI; LAN reverts to 192.168.1.1. Browse there and log in with admin/pfsense.
routers.source_name: Netgate 4100 Security Gateway — Initial Configuration (official documentation)

routers.credential_note: Mid-tier rack appliance in the 4100/6100/8200 family: a quad-core Atom CPU, two 10-Gigabit SFP+ uplinks, a pair of combo 1GbE ports and four 2.5GbE ports feed 8GB of RAM running pfSense Plus. Netgate's own initial-configuration docs confirm the shared factory login admin/pfsense; pfSense Plus 24.03 onward requires replacing that password before continuing.
routers.reset_steps: Boot to the serial console and pick 'Reset to factory defaults', or from the pfSense GUI go to Diagnostics > Factory Defaults — either path drops the LAN interface back to 192.168.1.1 for the admin/pfsense login.
routers.source_name: Netgate 6100 Security Gateway — Initial Configuration (official documentation)

routers.credential_note: Flagship of the trio: eight Atom C3758R cores, two 10-Gigabit SFP+ ports, two combo 1GbE ports and four 2.5GbE ports back a 16GB RAM budget for pfSense Plus, well ahead of the 4100/6100 in throughput. Netgate's official initial-configuration guide lists the same factory credential as the rest of the line — admin/pfsense — with pfSense Plus 24.03+ requiring an immediate change.
routers.reset_steps: Restore factory settings via the console/serial boot menu (option 4) or Diagnostics > Factory Defaults inside pfSense; the LAN side comes back up at 192.168.1.1 for the admin/pfsense login.
routers.source_name: Netgate 8200 Security Gateway — Initial Configuration (official documentation)

routers.credential_note: Entry-level pfSense Plus security-gateway/firewall (Marvell ARM, 3x Gigabit Ethernet, fanless). Genuine static default admin/pfsense; a password change is forced at first login on pfSense Plus 24.03 and later.
routers.reset_steps: On the SG-1100 the recessed reset button is a HARD reset (it powers the unit off immediately) and is NOT a factory-default reset — Netgate warns it can corrupt data. Restore defaults via the console menu or the GUI at Diagnostics > Factory Defaults instead. Then browse to https://192.168.1.1 and sign in.
routers.source_name: Netgate 1100 Security Gateway Manual (official)

routers.credential_note: pfSense Plus security-gateway/firewall appliance (Marvell ARM, multi-Gigabit, optional embedded LTE). Genuine static default admin/pfsense; on pfSense Plus 24.03 and later you must change this to a non-default password at first login.
routers.reset_steps: The recessed reset button restores factory defaults but only responds during the boot sequence (not while running); alternatively use the console menu or the GUI at Diagnostics > Factory Defaults. Then browse to https://192.168.1.1 and sign in.
routers.source_name: Netgate 2100 Security Gateway Manual (official)

routers.credential_note: NETGEAR documents a static default of admin / password (case-sensitive) for its CM-series cable modems. This applies to CM400/500/600/700/1000/1100/1200 and similar — but NOT the CM2000, which ships with a unique label password instead.
routers.reset_steps: The CM1000 is a cable modem only and broadcasts no Wi-Fi. Open a browser to http://192.168.100.1 and log in with username 'admin' and password 'password' (both case-sensitive). To factory reset, press and hold the Restore Factory Settings button with a paperclip for about 7 seconds until the power LED blinks, then log in again with admin/password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR Support (How do I log in to my NETGEAR cable modem)

routers.credential_note: Unlike other NETGEAR CM-series modems, the CM2000 has NO shared default password — each unit ships with a unique password printed on its label. NETGEAR calls this out explicitly.
routers.reset_steps: The CM2000 is a cable modem only. Open a browser to http://192.168.100.1 and log in with username 'admin' and the unique password printed on the product label. To factory reset, press and hold the Restore Factory Settings button with a paperclip for about 7 seconds until the power LED blinks; the login reverts to admin + the label's unique password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR Support (How do I log in to my NETGEAR cable modem)

routers.credential_note: DOCSIS 3.1, up to 2.5 Gbps port speed — a newer, higher-tier modem-only SKU than the CM1000/CM2000 already covered. NETGEAR's cable-modem login KB explicitly lists CM3000 among the applicable models and states the shared static default (admin/password); the CM2000 is called out by name as the sole exception with a unique label password — CM3000 is not exempted.
routers.reset_steps: The CM3000 is a DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem only (no built-in router/Wi-Fi, fixed LAN IP). Open a browser to http://192.168.100.1 and log in with username 'admin' and password 'password' (case-sensitive). To factory reset, press and hold the Restore Factory Settings button with a paperclip for about 7 seconds until the power LED blinks, then log in again with admin/password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR Support — How do I log in to my NETGEAR cable modem? (CM3000 listed under Applicable Models)

routers.credential_note: NETGEAR's own DGN2200 user manual states the modem router ships with the user name admin and password password and advises changing them. Genuine documented static default for this DSL gateway.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser to http://192.168.0.1 (or http://routerlogin.net) and log in with admin / password. To reset, hold the Restore Factory Settings button on the rear for about 7 seconds until the LEDs blink, then release; the login reverts to admin / password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR DGN2200 User Manual (official PDF)

routers.credential_note: Multi-Gig DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem (32x8) with 2x 1G Ethernet aggregation — no Wi-Fi. Unlike NETGEAR's routers, its cable modems keep a genuine static default: admin / password (case-sensitive). NETGEAR: "The user name is admin. The default password is password."
routers.reset_steps: Use a paperclip to hold the rear Reset button ~7 seconds until the LEDs blink to restore factory defaults; credentials return to admin / password and the LAN IP to 192.168.100.1.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR CM1200 User Manual — official PDF

routers.credential_note: The Nighthawk app forces you to set your own admin password during setup — admin/password is not a working default. Web admin at routerlogin.net uses whatever password you created in the app.
routers.reset_steps: This WiFi 6 mesh kit is set up through the Nighthawk app, which makes you create an admin password, so there is no default web login. To reset the router unit, power it on and hold the Reset button on the back for about 7 seconds until the LED blinks, then re-run setup via the Nighthawk app or http://routerlogin.net to create a new password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR KB 1148 — Default user interface passwords for NETGEAR devices

routers.credential_note: Documented default is admin / password. Later revisions (e.g. R6700v3) may prompt you to set an admin password on first setup.
routers.reset_steps: Go to http://www.routerlogin.net (192.168.1.1) with admin / password. To reset, hold the Restore Factory Settings button with a paperclip ~7 seconds until the Power LED blinks amber.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR official KB 1148 (Default UI passwords)

routers.credential_note: A pre-forced-setup-era model: default login is admin / password.
routers.reset_steps: Go to http://www.routerlogin.net (192.168.1.1) with admin / password. To reset, use a paperclip to hold the Restore Factory Settings button ~7 seconds until the Power LED blinks.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR official KB 24340 (R7000 factory defaults)

routers.credential_note: Modern Nighthawk firmware makes you set your own admin password on first setup — there is no admin/admin or admin/password that works out of the box. Netgear's legacy default (admin / password) only applies to older models.
routers.reset_steps: This tri-band Nighthawk forces you to create an admin password (and security questions) during first-time setup, so there is no working factory login to recover. To start clean, power the router on, find the recessed Reset button on the back, and press and hold it with a paperclip for about 7 seconds until the Power LED blinks. After it reboots, browse to http://routerlogin.net (or 192.168.1.1) and the setup wizard walks you through creating a new admin password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR KB 1148 — Default user interface passwords for NETGEAR devices

routers.credential_note: Dual-band Wi-Fi 6 (AX2400), 5-stream, 2.4/5 GHz standalone router with four gigabit LAN ports — an entry AX SKU below the AX3000 RAX40 and AX4300 RAX43/RAX45. Web login at routerlogin.net (192.168.1.1); no universal default password. NETGEAR's manual: "The password is the one that you specified the first time that you logged in."
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button on the rear panel for at least 7 seconds until the Power LED blinks, then release to restore factory default settings.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR Nighthawk AX2400 WiFi 6 Router (RAX30) User Manual — official

routers.credential_note: Nighthawk AX4 4-stream dual-band Wi-Fi 6 (AX3000), 2.4/5 GHz standalone router, four gigabit LAN + one gigabit WAN — sits between the AX2400 RAX30 and the AX4300 RAX43/RAX45 already covered. NETGEAR's manual: "The password is the one that you specified the first time that you logged in."
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button on the rear panel until the Power LED blinks, then release to return the router to factory default settings.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR Nighthawk AX4 AX3000 WiFi Router (RAX40) User Manual — official

routers.credential_note: This WiFi 6 Nighthawk forces you to choose your own admin password at setup — there is no admin/password out of the box. A factory reset is the only way back in if you forget it.
routers.reset_steps: The RAX43 requires you to create an admin password during first-time setup. To regain access, power the router on, hold the recessed Reset button on the rear with a paperclip for about 7 seconds until the Power LED blinks, then after it reboots visit http://routerlogin.net (192.168.1.1) and set a new admin password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR KB 1148 — Default user interface passwords for NETGEAR devices

routers.credential_note: Nighthawk AX6 (AX4300-class) dual-band Wi-Fi 6 router, 4 external antennas, 4x gigabit LAN + 1 gigabit WAN — distinct SKU from the RAX43/RAX50/RAX70/RAX80 already covered. NETGEAR's own login KB: username is admin, password is the one you specified during setup — no factory default password.
routers.reset_steps: Use a paperclip to press and hold the recessed Reset button on the rear panel for about 7 seconds until the power LED blinks amber, then release.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR Support — How do I log in to my NETGEAR home router? (applies to Nighthawk RAX45)

routers.credential_note: Username is admin. Newer NETGEAR products require setting the admin password on first setup, so there is no usable factory-default password.
routers.reset_steps: Go to http://www.routerlogin.net (192.168.1.1); newer NETGEAR products require you to set the admin password during first-time setup. To reset, hold the Reset button ~10 seconds until the Power LED blinks.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR official KB 1148 (Default UI passwords)

routers.credential_note: Nighthawk AX6 6-stream AX5400 dual-band Wi-Fi 6 router. The username is fixed at admin, but there is no static default password — it is the one you create at first login. NETGEAR: "The user name is admin. The password is the one that you specified the first time that you logged in."
routers.reset_steps: Use a paperclip to hold the rear Reset button until the Power LED blinks, then release to restore factory defaults; you set a new admin password at the next login.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR Nighthawk RAX54S User Manual — official PDF

routers.credential_note: Newer Nighthawk firmware makes you set the admin password at first setup, so admin/password is not a valid default. Reset to factory only if you've lost the password you created.
routers.reset_steps: Setup on this tri-band Nighthawk forces you to pick an admin password, so there is no factory login to fall back on. To reset, power it on, press and hold the Reset button on the back for roughly 7 seconds until the Power LED flashes, wait for reboot, then open http://routerlogin.net or 192.168.1.1 and create a new admin password in the wizard.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR KB 1148 — Default user interface passwords for NETGEAR devices

routers.credential_note: This model prompts you to create an admin password during initial setup — the old admin/password default does not apply. If you never changed it, a factory reset lets you set a new one.
routers.reset_steps: The Nighthawk AX8 setup wizard requires you to create your own admin password at first login, so recover access by factory resetting rather than hunting a default. Power the unit on, hold the recessed Reset button on the rear panel for about 7 seconds until the Power LED blinks, then let it reboot and go to http://routerlogin.net (192.168.1.1) to set a fresh admin password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR KB 1148 — Default user interface passwords for NETGEAR devices

routers.credential_note: Tri-band Wi-Fi 6E (AXE7800) standalone desktop router, 2.4/5/6 GHz, with a 2.5G Multi-Gig Internet port, four gigabit LAN and USB-C 3.0 — a 6GHz tier above the dual-band RAX30/RAX40 in this run. The factory label prints admin/password, but NETGEAR's own manual states the live login is the one you set on first login: "The password is the one that you specified the first time that you logged in."
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the recessed Reset button on the rear panel for at least 10 seconds until the Power LED blinks white, then release to restore factory settings.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR Nighthawk AXE7800 RAXE300 User Manual (202-12252-01) — official

routers.credential_note: Tri-band WiFi 6E flagship. The login name is admin, but there is no usable factory password — newer NETGEAR products force you to set the admin password on first setup (routerlogin.net or the Nighthawk app).
routers.reset_steps: Insert a paperclip into the recessed Reset hole on the back and hold about 7 seconds until the Power LED blinks amber, then release; the AXE11000 reboots to factory defaults and prompts you to create the admin password during first-time setup.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR official KB 1148 (Default UI passwords)

routers.credential_note: BE19000 WiFi 7 tower router (sold as RS700 / RS700S). Login name admin; no default password ships — first-time setup requires you to create one. Manage at routerlogin.net or in the Nighthawk app.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the recessed Reset button with a pin for roughly 7 seconds until the Power LED starts blinking, then release to restore factory defaults; you choose the admin password when the setup wizard runs.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR official KB 1148 (Default UI passwords)

routers.credential_note: Netgear documents the Orbi default admin login as admin / password. If you set the system up through the Orbi app you may have been prompted to create your own password instead — in that case reset to factory to restore admin/password.
routers.reset_steps: Log in to the router (RBR50) at http://orbilogin.com or 192.168.1.1 with user name admin and password password (case-sensitive). To factory reset, power the Orbi router on and hold the Reset button on the bottom for about 7-10 seconds until the ring LED blinks amber, then re-sync the satellite and log in with admin/password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR KB 31014 — Change your Orbi WiFi System's admin login password

routers.credential_note: Set up through the Orbi app, this system forces you to create your own admin password. Netgear's legacy Orbi default (admin / password) may still apply if configured via the web interface, but app setup overrides it.
routers.reset_steps: This WiFi 6 Orbi is normally set up via the Orbi app, which makes you create an admin password, so there's no reliable default. To reset the router (RBR750), power it on and hold the Reset button on the bottom for about 7-10 seconds until the ring LED blinks amber, then re-run setup in the Orbi app or at http://orbilogin.com to set a new admin password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR KB 31014 — Change your Orbi WiFi System's admin login password

routers.credential_note: Tri-band Wi-Fi 6 Orbi mesh system (RBR760 router + RBS760 satellite), AX5400 class. Username is admin with no static default password — it is the one you set the first time you log in at orbilogin.com. NETGEAR: "The user name is admin. The password is the one that you specified the first time that you logged in."
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button on the bottom of the RBR760 router until the LED flashes to restore factory defaults; you then set a new admin password during setup.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR Orbi RBR760/RBS760 User Manual — official PDF

routers.credential_note: Orbi app setup forces you to set your own admin password, so there's no admin/password out of the box. The legacy Orbi default (admin / password) only applies to web-interface configuration.
routers.reset_steps: This WiFi 6 Orbi kit is configured through the Orbi app, which makes you create an admin password during setup. To reset the router (RBR760), power it on and hold the Reset button on the bottom for about 7-10 seconds until the ring LED blinks amber, then re-run setup in the Orbi app or at http://orbilogin.com to choose a new admin password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR KB 31014 — Change your Orbi WiFi System's admin login password

routers.credential_note: App-based setup forces you to create your own admin password on this model — admin/password is not guaranteed to work. Netgear's Orbi KB still lists admin / password as the documented default for web-interface setups.
routers.reset_steps: The Orbi AX6000 is set up through the Orbi app, which requires you to create an admin password, so there is no working default login. To reset the router (RBR850), power it on and hold the Reset button on the bottom for about 7-10 seconds until the ring LED blinks amber, then re-run setup via the Orbi app or http://orbilogin.com and set a new password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR KB 31014 — Change your Orbi WiFi System's admin login password

routers.credential_note: Tri-band Wi-Fi 6 (AX6000-class) mesh system — RBR850 router + 2x RBS850 satellites with a dedicated backhaul band — a 3-piece pack distinct from the 2-piece RBK852 bundle already covered. NETGEAR's Orbi setup KB: create your own administrator password; the default admin login is 'admin' with no factory password.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button on the back of the Orbi router for about 7 seconds until the LED blinks, then re-pair satellites using the Orbi app or orbilogin.com.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR Support — How do I set up my Orbi WiFi System? (applies to RBK853)

routers.credential_note: This older AC1200 model ships with Netgear's universal default: user name admin, password password. Change it immediately after logging in, since it is publicly documented.
routers.reset_steps: Log in at http://routerlogin.net or 192.168.1.1 with user name admin and password password (both case-sensitive). If those don't work, power the router on, use a paperclip to press and hold the Restore Factory Settings button on the back for about 7 seconds until the Power LED blinks, then log in with admin/password after it reboots.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR KB 1148 — Default user interface passwords for NETGEAR devices

routers.credential_note: The R6260 uses Netgear's documented default of admin / password. It's a universal default, not unique to your unit, so replace it right after first login.
routers.reset_steps: Browse to http://routerlogin.net or 192.168.1.1 and sign in with user name admin and password password (case-sensitive). To factory reset, power the router on, hold the recessed Restore Factory Settings button on the back for about 7 seconds until the Power LED blinks, then log back in with admin/password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR KB 1148 — Default user interface passwords for NETGEAR devices

routers.credential_note: This older Nighthawk AC1900 predates forced-setup firmware, so admin / password is the real documented default. It's the same on every unit — change it immediately.
routers.reset_steps: Open http://routerlogin.net or 192.168.1.1 and log in with user name admin and password password (both case-sensitive). If the password was changed and forgotten, power the router on and hold the Restore Factory Settings button on the back for about 7 seconds until the Power LED blinks, then use admin/password after it restarts.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR KB 1148 — Default user interface passwords for NETGEAR devices

routers.credential_note: A classic N600 dual-band model whose officially documented default is admin / password (case-sensitive). NETGEAR's KB notes newer models require a password to be set on first login — this older one does not.
routers.reset_steps: Go to http://routerlogin.net or http://192.168.1.1 and sign in with admin / password. To factory reset, hold the Restore Factory Settings button on the underside for about 7 seconds until the power light blinks, then release and wait for reboot; login returns to admin / password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR Support KB 1148 — Default UI passwords

routers.credential_note: The documented factory default for this older gigabit N600 is admin / password. NETGEAR's official KB is the source; newer NETGEAR firmware forces a password at setup, but this model shipped with the static default.
routers.reset_steps: Browse to http://routerlogin.net or http://192.168.1.1 and log in with admin / password. Factory reset: press and hold the Restore Factory Settings button on the back for about 7 seconds until the power LED flashes, then release; defaults revert to admin / password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR Support KB 1148 — Default UI passwords

routers.credential_note: This is an older NETGEAR model, so the documented factory default is admin / password (very old NETGEAR units used 1234). NETGEAR's official KB confirms these defaults; note that NETGEAR's newer routers instead force you to create a password on first setup.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser to http://routerlogin.net or http://192.168.1.1 and log in with admin / password. If that fails, factory reset: with the router powered on, press and hold the Restore Factory Settings button on the back for about 7 seconds until the power LED blinks, then release; the credentials revert to admin / password.
routers.source_name: NETGEAR Support KB 1148 — Default UI passwords

routers.credential_note: Netis does not publish a single universal web-login default. Official support documents the admin page at 192.168.1.1 / netis.cc and a default Wi-Fi password of 'password'; the login credentials are on the device label. Many older Netis units used guest/guest, but that is not guaranteed - check the label.
routers.reset_steps: Reset: with the router powered on, press and hold the Default/RESET button for about 10 seconds until it reboots, then release. Browse to http://192.168.1.1 or http://netis.cc and sign in using the credentials printed on the device's bottom label.
routers.source_name: Netis Official Support FAQ

routers.credential_note: Per Nokia's official Help Center, the admin password is the unique value printed on the sticker of the root Beacon — there is no universal default. The username is admin; the password is per-device.
routers.reset_steps: Nokia WiFi Beacons are set up through the Nokia WiFi app. You can also sign in to the app or the web GUI with the admin credentials printed on the sticker of the root (primary) Beacon — you must be connected to the Nokia WiFi network. If you forget a changed admin password, recovery is not possible: press and hold the reset button on the root Beacon to factory reset, then redo setup in the app.
routers.source_name: Nokia WiFi Help Center — Sign in with admin credentials

routers.credential_note: VDSL/FTTC broadband hub issued by NOW (Sky's value brand, a Sky SR-series hub). Rare among ISP gear in having a genuinely STATIC published default — NOW's own help page states the login is admin / nowtv (lower case) at 192.168.0.1, not a per-unit label password. Users are told to change it immediately.
routers.reset_steps: Browse to http://192.168.0.1 and sign in with admin / nowtv (lower case), then open the Maintenance tab and choose Set Password. To factory reset, hold the recessed reset pinhole on the rear for about 10 seconds until the hub reboots.
routers.source_name: NOW Broadband Help — Change Admin Password For Your NOW Broadband Hub (official)

routers.credential_note: DSL/fibre gateway issued by o2 (Telefónica) Germany across the HomeBox line. The admin UI at o2.box (192.168.1.1) ships completely open from the factory — you create your own device password on first login, a genuine set-on-setup credential per o2's own router help page.
routers.reset_steps: Use a pen or similar object to press the recessed Reset opening on the back of the HomeBox and hold for about 10-15 seconds until the Power LED lights up red, then release and wait for the Power LED to return to solid green.
routers.source_name: o2 (Telefónica Deutschland) — Router-Hilfe (official)

routers.credential_note: There is no standalone web-admin login or default admin/password. Altice One gateways are cloud/account-managed — all settings live behind your Optimum ID at optimum.net/router or in the Optimum app.
routers.reset_steps: The Altice One / Optimum gateway is managed through your Optimum account, not a local admin password. Go to optimum.net/router (or the Optimum Support & WiFi app) and sign in with your Optimum ID and password to view devices and change the WiFi name/password and guest network. To factory reset the hardware, press and hold the recessed Reset button on the unit ~10 seconds until it reboots, then reconfigure through your Optimum account.
routers.source_name: Optimum — Altice One Settings

routers.credential_note: Australian Optus-supplied home internet gateway (Ultra WiFi Gen 2 on cable/NBN; the Nokia FastMile 5G Gateway variant on 5G FWA). Admin is reached at 192.168.0.1. Optus uses no universal default — enter the password printed on the sticker on the base of the modem into the password field (the Ultra WiFi has no separate username).
routers.reset_steps: Hold the recessed reset button on the rear/underside for a few seconds until the modem restarts; login reverts to the password printed on the base label. Note your OptusNet username/password first, as a reset wipes custom settings.
routers.source_name: Optus Official Support — Home Internet WiFi username & password help

routers.credential_note: Next-generation Livebox (post Livebox 4/5, already covered generically as 'orange-livebox') with an on-device touchscreen and app/QR login path. Username is admin; per Orange's official support, the default password is the first 8 characters of the Wi-Fi security key printed on the device label — not a shared static default.
routers.reset_steps: Touchscreen-equipped fibre gateway; alternative login via the 'Orange et moi' app or the QR code shown on the device's touchscreen (no password entry needed that way). Reset via the recessed button restores the label-derived default.
routers.source_name: Assistance Orange Pro — Livebox 6 et 7 : accéder à l'interface de configuration (official)

routers.credential_note: Username is 'admin'; the admin password is not a fixed default but the first 8 uppercase characters of the WiFi security key printed on the Livebox label. Orange recommends changing it after first login.
routers.reset_steps: To log in: connect to the Livebox, browse to 192.168.1.1 (or http://livebox), use username 'admin' and the admin password, which is the first 8 characters (uppercase, no spaces) of the WiFi security key printed on the Livebox label. To factory reset: with the Livebox on, press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back for about 10 seconds until it restarts, or use 'Mot de passe oublié' on the login page to reset the interface password.
routers.source_name: Assistance Orange — Livebox 6 et 7 : réinitialiser le mot de passe d'accès à l'interface

routers.credential_note: Dual-WAN business SD-WAN router: one Gigabit Ethernet WAN plus an embedded Cat-4/Cat-7 LTE modem and a FlexModule slot; the Wi-Fi variant adds 802.11ac. Genuine static admin/admin default, and Peplink forces a password change on the first successful login. Confirm the LAN IP against the device label — the manual is Balance-line-generic.
routers.reset_steps: With a paperclip, press and hold the recessed reset button — ~5-10 seconds for an admin-password reset (status LED blinks red twice) or ~20 seconds for a full factory reset (blinks red three times) — then release. After reboot, browse to https://192.168.1.1 and log in.
routers.source_name: Peplink Balance User Manual, firmware 8.1.1 (official)

routers.credential_note: Enterprise/branch SD-WAN multi-WAN router (all-gigabit ports, 2.5 Gbps routing throughput, patented SpeedFusion bonding), managed via the on-box Web Admin Interface or InControl2 cloud. Genuine documented static default admin/admin; the manual recommends but does not force a change. Read-only account is user/user.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the recessed reset button on the unit to restore factory defaults, which returns the Web Admin login to admin/admin at http://192.168.1.1. Change the Admin/Read-only passwords under System > Admin Security.
routers.source_name: Peplink Balance User Manual (Firmware 6.1) — download.peplink.com (official)

routers.credential_note: Mid-tier multi-WAN SD-WAN router/firewall (configurable gigabit WAN/LAN ports, SpeedFusion bonding) positioned above the Balance 310X already covered, for medium-business deployments. Genuine documented static default admin/admin; read-only account is user/user.
routers.reset_steps: With a paperclip, press and hold the recessed reset button on the back panel for about 10-20 seconds until all LEDs flash, then release to restore factory defaults; from firmware 5.4+ the admin password alone can also be reset via Maintenance > Reset Admin Password on the front LCD panel. Browse to http://192.168.1.1 and log in with admin/admin.
routers.source_name: Peplink Balance User Manual v6.1 — download.peplink.com (official)

routers.credential_note: Dual-WAN SD-WAN router (Ethernet + optional embedded cellular) for SMB/branch use, desktop form factor with no built-in Wi-Fi radio — Peplink's entry point above the Balance 20X. Genuine static default admin/admin confirmed in the official Balance series manual.
routers.reset_steps: With a paperclip, press and hold the recessed reset button on the back panel for about 10-20 seconds until all LEDs flash, then release to restore factory defaults. Browse to https://192.168.1.1 and log in with admin/admin.
routers.source_name: Peplink Balance Multi-WAN Bonding Routers User Manual v6.1 (official)

routers.credential_note: Compact mobile 4G/LTE cellular router/gateway with a single embedded modem, DIN-rail or wall mountable for vehicle/IoT deployments. Genuine static default admin/admin confirmed in the official Pepwave MAX firmware manual, on a distinct default LAN IP (192.168.50.1) from the Balance line.
routers.reset_steps: With a paperclip, press and hold the recessed reset button for about 10-20 seconds until all LEDs flash, then release to restore factory defaults. Browse to https://192.168.50.1 and log in with admin/admin.
routers.source_name: Pepwave MAX Series Firmware Manual fw7 (official)

routers.credential_note: Rugged dual-SIM/dual-cellular Pepwave MAX router for M2M and fixed-site failover (on-board Wi-Fi AP, gigabit Ethernet WAN/LAN), documented in the MAX Series User Manual 8.4.0 section 2.44. Managed via the on-box Web Admin or InControl2 cloud. The static admin/admin default is transient — first logon mandates a password change.
routers.reset_steps: Rugged dual-cellular M2M/fleet LTE router. Press and hold the reset button to restore factory defaults; the Web Admin returns to admin/admin at http://192.168.50.1, after which the firmware forces a new 10-character password (mixed case plus a digit) on first logon.
routers.source_name: Pepwave MAX Series User Manual 8.4.0 — download.peplink.com (official)

routers.credential_note: Ruggedized dual-embedded-cellular-modem router for vehicle/vessel mounting — the higher-throughput 'Pro' tier of the MAX BR2 line already covered. Genuine documented static default admin/admin in the Pepwave MAX manual, same forced-change behavior as the base BR2.
routers.reset_steps: With a paperclip, press and hold the recessed reset button for about 10-20 seconds until all LEDs flash, then release to restore factory defaults. Browse to http://192.168.50.1 and log in with admin/admin, after which the firmware forces a new password.
routers.source_name: Pepwave MAX User Manual v6.1 — download.peplink.com (official)

routers.credential_note: Pepwave MAX Transit cellular router built for vehicles and public transit (integrated GPS, Wi-Fi AP, gigabit Ethernet), covered by the MAX Series User Manual 8.4.0 Transit variant sections. Runs from the local Web Admin or InControl2. Ships with the documented admin/admin default but compels an immediate password change at first successful login.
routers.reset_steps: In-vehicle transit cellular router with GPS. Hold the recessed reset button until the unit reboots to factory settings; login reverts to admin/admin at http://192.168.50.1 and you must define a fresh password (minimum ten characters, upper and lower case, including a number) before the dashboard loads.
routers.source_name: Pepwave MAX Series User Manual 8.4.0 — download.peplink.com (official)

routers.credential_note: SOHO router with a simultaneous dual-band 802.11ac access point, 4x Gigabit Ethernet, USB LTE/3G failover WAN and three dual-band SMA antennas. Genuine static admin/admin default; Peplink forces a password change on the first successful login. Default LAN IP is 192.168.50.1.
routers.reset_steps: Locate the reset button on the back panel; with a paperclip press and hold it ~10 seconds for a factory reset (status LED turns red), then release. After reboot, browse to https://192.168.50.1 and log in.
routers.source_name: Pepwave Surf SOHO User Manual, firmware 8.3.0 (official)

routers.credential_note: No universal default. The Plusnet Hub One uses username 'admin' plus a unique admin password printed on the back-of-hub card/sticker.
routers.reset_steps: To log in: connect to the hub, browse to 192.168.1.254, enter username 'admin' and the Hub admin password from the card/sticker on the back of the hub. To factory reset: with the hub powered on, press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back for about 20 seconds until the lights flash; the admin password returns to the value printed on the back.
routers.source_name: Plusnet Help — How to use your Plusnet router (Hub One)

routers.credential_note: No universal default password. Each Hub Two ships with a unique admin password printed on a card/sticker on the back of the hub; the username is 'admin'.
routers.reset_steps: To log in: connect to the hub, browse to 192.168.1.254, enter username 'admin' and the Hub admin password printed on the card/sticker on the back of the hub. To factory reset: with the hub on, press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back for about 20 seconds until the lights flash and it reboots; the admin password reverts to the one printed on the back.
routers.source_name: Plusnet Help — How to use your Plusnet router (Hub Two)

routers.credential_note: No admin/admin. The Reyee EW series ships with no preset admin password - on first login at 192.168.110.1 / ruiyi.cn you configure directly and set your own management password.
routers.reset_steps: Reset: with the router powered on, press and hold the RESET button for about 10 seconds until the system LED blinks, then release and wait for reboot. Browse to http://192.168.110.1 or ruiyi.cn and set a new management password during the wizard.
routers.source_name: Ruijie Networks Official - Reyee RG-EW Series Home Wi-Fi Routers FAQs

routers.credential_note: Canadian cable (DOCSIS 3.1) gateway used on Rogers Ignite Internet. Unlike most ISP gateways this one ships with a documented static admin login — username Cusadmin, password password (or your Easy Connect Wi-Fi password) — reached at 192.168.0.1. The newer Xfinity-platform Ignite WiFi Gateway (XB6/7/8) is instead app-managed and has no equivalent published web-admin default.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the recessed reset button on the back of the Hitron CODA modem ~10-15 seconds until it restarts; login returns to Cusadmin / password.
routers.source_name: Rogers Official Support — Sign into and change the password of your Hitron CODA modem

routers.credential_note: Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) 2x2:2 indoor access point that can also run in RUCKUS Unleashed controller-less mesh mode. A standalone, never-configured AP falls back to the documented static factory login super/sp-admin; once joined to an Unleashed network, admin credentials instead come from the network-wide account chosen during the Unleashed setup wizard.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the recessed Reset button (use a paperclip) for 8-10 seconds until the AP reboots, or over SSH run 'set factory' followed by 'reboot'.
routers.source_name: Ruckus/CommScope Support KB 000012418 — How to factory reset or factory default different types of Ruckus Access Points (official)

routers.credential_note: Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) indoor access point run in Ruckus's controller-less 'Unleashed' mode — distinct from the standalone-mode static super/sp-admin default already covered for the R350. Ruckus's own knowledge base: the AP boots broadcasting an unencrypted 'Configure.Me-[xxxxxx]' SSID and setup completes at unleashed.ruckuswireless.com; admin credentials are created during that first-run wizard, not a static factory default.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the reset pinhole for about 20 seconds until the LEDs cycle to restore factory defaults; the AP re-broadcasts the temporary 'Configure.Me-[xxxxxx]' SSID for a fresh setup.
routers.source_name: Ruckus Knowledge Base 000006019 — Default IP address for Ruckus devices (official)

routers.credential_note: Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) 3200M dual-band gigabit mesh router (2402 Mbps 5GHz + 800 Mbps 2.4GHz), 5 gigabit Ethernet ports, 8 external antennas; managed via ReyeeOS eWeb or the Reyee Router app. No universal default — the per-device password is on the bottom nameplate (if none is shown, admin is used), and the setup wizard mandates a reset on first login. Corrects the common aggregator claim of admin/admin.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button for more than 10 seconds to restore factory settings; then log in at http://192.168.110.1 with the per-unit default password printed on the bottom nameplate (format Rexxxxxx). The wizard forces a new eWeb password on first login.
routers.source_name: Ruijie Reyee RG-EW3200GX PRO ReyeeOS 1.380 Configuration Guide (V1.0) — reyee.ruijie.com (official)

routers.credential_note: Reyee mesh Wi-Fi router — distinct mesh-category hardware from the already-covered RG-EW1200G/RG-EW3200GX PRO single routers. No preset admin/password pair: first connection to 192.168.110.1 auto-loads the configuration wizard where the owner creates the management password.
routers.reset_steps: Wi-Fi 6 mesh router (ReyeeOS). Hold the Reset pinhole for about 10 seconds until all LEDs flash, then reconnect to the default @Ruijie-sXXXX SSID and run the setup wizard again to create a new management password.
routers.source_name: Ruijie Reyee RG-M32 Mesh Router ReyeeOS 1.317/1.313/1.308 Configuration Guide — reyee.ruijie.com (official)

routers.credential_note: SaskTel-issued ARRIS gateway, distinct from Ziply Fiber's NVG448BQ already covered (different ISP, different SKU suffix). Username defaults to admin; password is unique per unit from the bottom label.
routers.reset_steps: SaskTel infiNET fibre gateway (ARRIS NVG448, not the -BQ variant). A factory reset restores the same Device Access Code printed on a label on the bottom of the unit.
routers.source_name: SaskTel Support — Logging in to your ARRIS NVG448 gateway (official)

routers.credential_note: SaskTel fusion Internet gateway — genuine shared static default admin/admin explicitly documented by SaskTel support, unlike the label-unique fibre gateways above.
routers.reset_steps: SaskTel fusion Internet fixed-wireless gateway (Green Packet). A reset via the recessed button restores the documented static admin/admin pair; change it under Settings > Management > Password Setting.
routers.source_name: SaskTel Support — Logging in to your Green Packet gateway (fusion Internet service) (official)

routers.credential_note: SaskTel Huawei fusion Internet gateway with its own vendor-specific static default (LTEcpe), distinct from the Green Packet gateway's admin/admin above.
routers.reset_steps: SaskTel fusion Internet fixed-wireless gateway (Huawei B2268H, also reachable at 172.16.1.254). The reset button restores the documented static admin/LTEcpe pair; you're prompted to set a new password on first login.
routers.source_name: SaskTel Support — Logging in to your Huawei B2268H gateway (fusion Internet service) (official)

routers.credential_note: SaskTel-issued fibre gateway. Username auto-fills as admin; password is device-unique, taken from the serial-number label, distinct from SaskTel's other fusion Internet fixed-wireless gateways below.
routers.reset_steps: SaskTel infiNET fibre gateway (Vantiva/Technicolor EGA228B). A factory reset restores the same unique Web UI Password / 20-character Device Access Code printed on the gateway's serial-number label — it does not reveal a shared admin/admin.
routers.source_name: SaskTel Support — Logging in to your Vantiva EGA228B gateway (official)

routers.credential_note: Username is 'admin', but the password is the unique WiFi password printed on the base of the hub — not a fixed default. Older Sky Hub / Sky Q Hub models historically used admin/sky; the current Sky Broadband Hub uses the label WiFi password instead.
routers.reset_steps: To log in: connect to your Sky network, browse to 192.168.0.1, use username 'admin' and enter your WiFi password (the one printed on the base of the hub) when prompted. To factory reset: press and hold the recessed Reset/WPS pinhole on the back for around 30 seconds until the hub restarts; network name and password revert to the values on the base sticker.
routers.source_name: Sky Help — Access your Sky Broadband Hub settings

routers.credential_note: Spectrum's own Sagemcom/Askey units print the default sign-in on the rear label; older models used admin/admin but current RAC2V1K/RAC2V1S routers are largely locked to the My Spectrum app, so the web tool is view-only for many settings.
routers.reset_steps: Connect to the router and browse to http://192.168.1.1. Sign in with username 'admin'; the password is printed on the label on the back of the router. Newer Spectrum routers restrict most settings — use the My Spectrum app or spectrum.net to change the WiFi name/password. To factory reset, press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back ~10 seconds until the lights cycle, then sign in with the label credentials.
routers.source_name: Spectrum Support — Managing WiFi Router Settings

routers.credential_note: Starlink's LEO-satellite Wi-Fi router (Gen 2 tri-band router / Gen 3 Wi-Fi 6 mesh, ships with the dish kit). It has no administrator web portal — there is no admin username or password to set; SSID, password and bypass mode are configured exclusively in the Starlink mobile app. MAC filtering and port forwarding are not offered.
routers.reset_steps: There is no web admin login. Change all settings in the Starlink app (Settings). To factory reset, use the app's reset option or perform the physical reset for your router generation, then re-run setup in the app.
routers.source_name: Starlink Help Center — Does Starlink have a WiFi router administrator portal? (official)

routers.credential_note: No factory default login — SRM makes you create the admin account on first setup, so there is nothing like admin/admin. The MR2200ac can also be configured through the Synology DS router app.
routers.reset_steps: Connect by Ethernet, or join WiFi SSID Synology_(Serial) with password 'synology' (or set it up in the DS router mobile app). Browse to http://router.synology.com (or http://192.168.1.1:8000); the SRM wizard prompts you to create your own administrator account. To reset, hold RESET ~4 seconds (soft) or ~10 seconds (full factory reset) until it reboots.
routers.source_name: Synology — MR2200ac Hardware Installation Guide (PDF)

routers.credential_note: There is no factory admin password. Synology Router Manager (SRM) makes you create the administrator account during first-time setup, so the login is whatever you chose. Synology also recommends deactivating the default 'admin' username and using a custom one.
routers.reset_steps: Connect a computer by Ethernet, or join WiFi SSID Synology_(Serial) with password 'synology'. Open a browser and go to http://router.synology.com (or http://192.168.1.1:8000). The SRM setup wizard prompts you to create your own administrator account (username + password) on first run. To factory reset, press and hold the RESET button ~4 seconds for a soft reset (network/password) or ~10 seconds for a full factory reset until the router beeps/reboots.
routers.source_name: Synology — RT2600ac Hardware Installation Guide (PDF)

routers.credential_note: No default password ships on the RT6600ax. SRM forces you to set the administrator account during setup, so credentials are user-created. Avoid reusing 'admin'/'root' as the username per Synology's own guidance.
routers.reset_steps: Connect by Ethernet, or join WiFi SSID Synology_(Serial) with password 'synology'. Browse to http://router.synology.com (or http://192.168.1.1:8000) and complete the SRM wizard, which prompts you to create your own administrator account. To reset, hold the RESET button ~4 seconds (soft: network/password) or ~10 seconds (full factory reset) until it reboots.
routers.source_name: Synology — RT6600ax Hardware Installation Guide (PDF)

routers.credential_note: No default password. Like all Synology routers running SRM, the WRX560 requires you to create the administrator account during first-time setup, so the login is user-defined rather than a factory default.
routers.reset_steps: Connect by Ethernet, or join WiFi SSID Synology_(Serial) with password 'synology'. Browse to http://router.synology.com (or http://192.168.1.1:8000) and complete the SRM setup wizard, which prompts you to create your own administrator account. To reset, hold the RESET button ~4 seconds (soft reset) or ~10 seconds (full factory reset) until the router reboots.
routers.source_name: Synology — SRM 1.3 Router User's Guide (PDF)

routers.credential_note: US 5G fixed-wireless home gateway. Primary setup and management is through the T-Life app with your T-Mobile ID — there is no universal admin password. A web GUI also exists at http://192.168.12.1 (username admin); its default admin password is the unique value on the device label (on Arcadyan/Nokia units, revealed via the on-screen 'Where is my password?' link).
routers.reset_steps: Hold the reset button on the gateway for ~10 seconds until it restarts. Primary management is re-run through the T-Life app; the web-GUI admin password reverts to the unique value printed on the device label.
routers.source_name: T-Mobile Official Support — T-Mobile Internet Gateway Setup

routers.credential_note: Login details are on the sticker under the removable settings card on the back of the hub. TalkTalk's own guidance notes that only older/generic units fall back to admin/admin — current Wi-Fi Hubs use the printed unique credentials.
routers.reset_steps: To log in: connect to the hub, browse to 192.168.1.1 and enter the username and password from the sticker underneath the removable settings card on the back of the Wi-Fi Hub. To factory reset: with the hub on, press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back for about 15 seconds until it restarts; credentials revert to the values on the back-of-hub sticker.
routers.source_name: TalkTalk Help & Support — Change your router admin password

routers.credential_note: Australian NBN/hybrid gateway (Technicolor/Netgear-built). Unlike the Gen 3, the Gen 2/1.1 uses a fixed documented admin login — username admin, password Telstra — reached at http://mymodem or http://192.168.0.1. Telstra advises changing it after setup.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the reset button on the back of the modem for about 10 seconds until it restarts; login returns to username admin / password Telstra.
routers.source_name: Telstra Official Support — How do I access and use my modem settings?

routers.credential_note: Australian NBN gateway (Frontier/Arcadyan-built). Reached at http://mymodem or http://192.168.0.1 with username admin — but unlike the Gen 2 there is no fixed password: the admin password is the unique Wi-Fi password printed on the sticker on the bottom of the modem.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the reset button on the back of the modem for about 10 seconds until it restarts; the admin password reverts to the Wi-Fi password printed on the base label.
routers.source_name: Telstra Official Support — How do I access and use my modem settings?

routers.credential_note: PureFibre/copper gateway supplied by TELUS across Canada. Admin UI at 192.168.1.254, username admin, password printed on the side of the modem under 'GUI Access' — device-unique, not a shared static default, per TELUS's own support article.
routers.reset_steps: Locate the grey Factory Reset button on the back of the device. Using a thin object (pushpin, paper clip, or toothpick), press and hold the reset button until the Internet light turns red, then release. The modem restarts automatically — allow up to 10 minutes.
routers.source_name: TELUS Business Support — Troubleshoot: Boost Wi-Fi (TELUS Wi-Fi Hub) (official)

routers.credential_note: No admin/admin default — on first access via tendawifi.com you create the admin password. Any aggregator listing admin/admin for Tenda is wrong for this model.
routers.reset_steps: With the router on, hold the RESET pinhole ~5–7 seconds until it reboots to factory defaults.
routers.source_name: Tenda official — How to login to the web management page

routers.credential_note: AC2100 dual-band hardware. Tenda ships no universal credential for the AC21 — the label on the back carries a Wireless Password unique to that unit, and that is what gets you through the very first login at tendawifi.com. The setup wizard then splits them: one password for the wireless, another for management.
routers.reset_steps: Reset: with the router powered on, hold the RESET pinhole down for roughly 5-8 seconds with a pin until the LEDs blink, release, then allow about a minute to reboot. Reconnect to the default Tenda_XXXXXX SSID using the rear-label password, open tendawifi.com or 192.168.0.1, and run the wizard to choose a fresh management password.
routers.source_name: Tenda Official Support - How to login to the web management page

routers.credential_note: No admin/admin default — the admin password is set on first access via tendawifi.com.
routers.reset_steps: With the router on, hold the RESET pinhole ~7 seconds until it reboots to factory defaults.
routers.source_name: Tenda official — How to login to the web management page

routers.credential_note: The AC8 is an AC1200 dual-band router. There is no admin/admin here: on current Tenda firmware the first browser session at tendawifi.com asks for the Wireless Password from the sticker on the router's rear, and the wizard that follows has you create separate WiFi and login passwords.
routers.reset_steps: Reset: with the router powered on, use a pin to press and hold the RESET hole for about 5-8 seconds until the LEDs blink, then release and wait ~1 minute for reboot. Rejoin the stock Tenda_XXXXXX network with the label password, browse to tendawifi.com or 192.168.0.1, and let the wizard set a new login password.
routers.source_name: Tenda Official Support - How to login to the web management page

routers.credential_note: Tenda's AX12 is WiFi 6 (AX1500/AX3000). No shared default password exists for it. The first management session at tendawifi.com is authenticated with the per-unit Wireless Password from the rear sticker, and you then define your own wireless and login passwords in the setup flow.
routers.reset_steps: Reset: with power on, hold the RESET pinhole with a pin for about 5-8 seconds until the LEDs blink, let go, and wait roughly a minute for the reboot. Reconnect to the default Tenda_XXXXXX network using the sticker password, load tendawifi.com or 192.168.0.1, and finish setup with a new login password.
routers.source_name: Tenda Official Support - How to login to the web management page

routers.credential_note: Tenda Nova mesh is set up through the Tenda WiFi app, not admin/admin. There is no universal web password; the app account and the label Wi-Fi password control access.
routers.reset_steps: Reset a node: press and hold its RESET button for about 8 seconds until the LED turns solid red, then release and wait for it to reboot to factory state. Re-add the node in the Tenda WiFi app to reconfigure the mesh.
routers.source_name: Tenda Official - How to Log into the Management Page/Web UI

routers.credential_note: The RX3 runs WiFi 6 at AX1800. Nothing like admin/admin exists on it. Its firmware gates the opening tendawifi.com login behind the Wireless Password unique to that unit, printed on the rear label; afterwards the wizard asks you for two new passwords, one wireless and one for logging in.
routers.reset_steps: Reset: while powered, insert a pin into the RESET hole and keep it held around 5-8 seconds until the LEDs blink. Release and give it a minute to come back. Join the factory Tenda_XXXXXX network with the label's password, go to tendawifi.com or 192.168.0.1, and complete the wizard with a new login password.
routers.source_name: Tenda Official Support - How to login to the web management page

routers.credential_note: Login credentials are unique per unit and printed on the base of the hub, not a shared static default. Three's official device support: 'Locate your hub's webUI login credentials. This can be found on the base of the hub.'
routers.reset_steps: ZTE-made 5G indoor hub (Qualcomm SDX55M modem, Wi-Fi 6, USB-C, 2x gigabit LAN, up to 32 connected devices). Three's own device support does not publish a reset-button procedure on this page — use the Three app or contact Three support to reset or retrieve credentials.
routers.source_name: Three Device Support — Three 5G Hub MC801A (official)

routers.credential_note: Totolink's official support documents a genuine universal default for this N-series: username admin and password admin at 192.168.1.1. Because it is public, change both immediately after logging in.
routers.reset_steps: Reset: with the router powered on, press and hold the RESET button for about 10 seconds until the LEDs blink, then release and wait for reboot. Browse to http://192.168.1.1, log in with admin / admin, then open Advanced Setup > System > Admin Setup to set new credentials.
routers.source_name: Totolink Official - How to modify the user name and password

routers.credential_note: Current v5 firmware requires creating a login password. Legacy hardware revisions (C7 v1–v4) historically shipped admin/admin, but that isn't stated on a single current official page.
routers.reset_steps: Log in at http://tplinkwifi.net; on current (v5) firmware you create a login password on first login. To reset, hold Reset until the Power LED blinks, then create a new password.
routers.source_name: TP-Link official Archer A7 & C7 (v5) User Guide (FAQ)

routers.credential_note: AX1500 is entry-level WiFi 6, and the Archer AX10 handles credentials the same way the rest of the range does: the first login is where you create the admin password, because current firmware carries none. Wireless SSID and key live on the underside label and are unrelated to that password.
routers.reset_steps: Powered up, press the recessed Reset button on the back with a pin and hold near 10 seconds until the LEDs blink; release and wait for the reboot to factory defaults. Reconnect using the underside label's wireless name and key, visit http://tplinkwifi.net or 192.168.0.1, and create the admin password anew.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official — Archer AX10 & AX1500 User Guide

routers.credential_note: You log in with the password you set for the router; there is no factory admin/admin.
routers.reset_steps: Visit http://tplinkwifi.net and create a login password on first setup. To reset, hold Reset until the LEDs turn on, then create a new password.
routers.source_name: TP-Link official Archer AX20 & AX1800 User Guide (FAQ)

routers.credential_note: An AX1800 dual-band WiFi 6 router with no shared password behind it. Current TP-Link firmware treats the first web login as a registration step — you define the admin password, and there is nothing to type in a username box. Wireless SSID and key are separate values, printed on the label beneath the chassis.
routers.reset_steps: While powered, push a pin into the recessed Reset button on the back and hold about 10 seconds; the LEDs blink, then release. A reboot returns factory defaults. Reconnect to the stock AX1800 network using the underside label, visit http://tplinkwifi.net or 192.168.0.1, and define the admin password once more.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — How to log in to the web management page

routers.credential_note: AX3000 dual-band Wi-Fi 6 router (Intel chipset, 4 external antennas, 4x gigabit LAN + 1 gigabit WAN) — distinct hardware from the Archer AX55 (Qualcomm chipset) already covered. Official user guide: log in at http://tplinkwifi.net with your TP-Link ID or the password you set for the router — no factory admin/admin.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the RESET button on the back of the router (recessed, use a pin) for about 5-10 seconds until the LEDs flash, then release to restore factory defaults.
routers.source_name: TP-Link official Archer AX50 V1 User Guide (FAQ)

routers.credential_note: Modern TP-Link firmware forces you to create an admin password on first login — there is no admin/admin default and no username field.
routers.reset_steps: Visit http://tplinkwifi.net and create an admin password on first setup. To reset, hold the Reset button until the Power LED blinks, then set a new password.
routers.source_name: TP-Link official support (FAQ 87 — Router Login)

routers.credential_note: AX3000 dual-band Multi-Gig Wi-Fi 6 router with a 2.5 Gbps port and USB 3.0 — the 'Pro' Multi-Gig variant, a distinct SKU from the Archer AX55 already covered. Ethernet-based; no admin/admin default — a login password is created on first setup with no username. TP-Link: "Visit http://tplinkwifi.net, and create a login password for secure management purposes."
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button until the Power LED blinks to restore factory defaults, then browse to http://tplinkwifi.net to create a new login password.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Archer AX55 Pro (US) V2.0 User Guide — official PDF

routers.credential_note: AX5400 dual-band Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) 6-stream router with Gigabit WAN/LAN (Ethernet, non-DSL). No admin/admin default — the web UI forces you to create a login password on first setup, with no username field. TP-Link: "Visit http://tplinkwifi.net, and create a login password for secure management purposes."
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button until the Power LED blinks to restore factory defaults, then visit http://tplinkwifi.net to create a new login password.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Archer AX72 V1 User Guide (official)

routers.credential_note: AX5400 puts the Archer AX73 in WiFi 6 territory, but its login model is the plain one: nothing ships preset. The create-password screen is the first thing the web UI shows, and whatever you type there is the password from then on. The bottom label carries only the wireless name and key, never the admin password.
routers.reset_steps: Switch the router on, insert a pin into the recessed Reset button on the back, and keep it down for around 10 seconds until the LEDs blink. Release and let it reboot to factory defaults. Get back on the default WiFi with the label credentials, go to http://tplinkwifi.net or 192.168.0.1, and set the admin password again.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — How to log in to the web management page

routers.credential_note: Archer AX90 is the non-gaming tri-band AX6600 sibling. Its web UI has no factory password to guess: the initial page asks you to establish one, with no username alongside. The label under the router lists the wireless name and key only.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the recessed Reset button roughly 10 seconds with a pin while the unit is running, and release at the LED blink. After the restart everything is back to factory defaults. Join the label-printed wireless network, browse to http://tplinkwifi.net or 192.168.0.1, and establish a new admin password.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — How to log in to the web management page

routers.credential_note: Official setup guide instructs you to create a login password for secure management; no default password, no username field.
routers.reset_steps: Visit http://tplinkwifi.net and create a login password for management on first setup. To reset, hold Reset until the LED blinks, then create a new password.
routers.source_name: TP-Link official Archer AXE75 v2 Installation & User Guide

routers.credential_note: The BE9300-class Archer BE550 is a WiFi 7 router whose admin password simply does not exist until you type it. TP-Link's current firmware opens on a password-creation prompt rather than a login box, and no username is involved. Bottom-label printing covers the wireless SSID and key, nothing more.
routers.reset_steps: Keep the recessed Reset button pressed with a pin for roughly 10 seconds while powered, releasing once the LEDs change. Factory defaults return after the reboot. Attach to the default wireless network shown on the bottom label, open http://tplinkwifi.net or 192.168.0.1, and type a new admin password at the prompt.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — How to log in to the web management page

routers.credential_note: BE19000 marks the Archer BE800 as WiFi 7 hardware. The login flow did not change with the generation: no default password ships, and the first time you reach the web UI it asks you to make one up.
