The wireless name and key printed on the bottom label are not the admin credential.
routers.reset_steps: With the router on, use a pin to hold the recessed Reset button for about 10 seconds until the LEDs change, then let go. It reboots to factory defaults. Reconnect over the default wireless network named on the bottom label, load http://tplinkwifi.net or 192.168.0.1, and make up a new admin password.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — How to log in to the web management page

routers.credential_note: This is an older model: the earliest firmware used admin / admin, but current firmware requires you to create your own admin password on first login. If admin/admin does not work, the router has already prompted for (and you set) a custom password. The default Wi-Fi details are on the bottom label.
routers.reset_steps: With the router powered on, use a pin to press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back for about 10 seconds until the LEDs blink, then release. The router reboots to factory defaults. Reconnect to the default Wi-Fi (SSID and password on the bottom label), open http://tplinkwifi.net or 192.168.0.1, and log in or create the admin password.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — How to log in to the web management page

routers.credential_note: Per TP-Link's official login guide, newer TP-Link models (including current Archer C5 firmware) require you to create a custom admin password on first login; only older units used admin / admin. When ACT Fibernet supplies an Archer C5 it may be pre-provisioned with an ISP-set password (commonly on the install slip), so admin/admin should not be assumed.
routers.reset_steps: Connect to the router by Wi-Fi (default network name/password are on the router label) or LAN, then open http://tplinkwifi.net or http://192.168.0.1 in a browser. On current firmware you are prompted to create your own admin password on first login — there is no admin/admin. If you forget it, press and hold the recessed RESET button for about 10 seconds until the router reboots, then reopen tplinkwifi.net and create a new password.
routers.source_name: TP-Link — How to Log In to Your TP-Link Router

routers.credential_note: The Archer C54 is an AC1200 dual-band unit. Its management password has no factory value: the first visit to the admin UI is a create-a-password screen, and there is no username field beside it. The wireless key you need to get onto the network in the first place is on the bottom label.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the recessed rear Reset button with a pin for about 10 seconds while the router is on, releasing when the LEDs blink. It restarts at factory defaults. Reconnect over the default AC1200 wireless network (name and key on the bottom label), open http://tplinkwifi.net or 192.168.0.1, and create a replacement admin password.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — How to log in to the web management page

routers.credential_note: Directories that print admin/admin for the Archer C6 are quoting a default this 802.11ac router never had. Firmware blocks you at the first login screen until you supply a password of your own choosing. Separately, the factory wireless SSID and its key are silkscreened on the sticker underneath.
routers.reset_steps: Power on, then hold the recessed Reset button on the back with a pin for roughly 10 seconds — release once the LEDs blink. Factory defaults come back after the reboot. Join the stock wireless network using the sticker credentials, load http://tplinkwifi.net or 192.168.0.1, and choose a fresh admin password at the prompt.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — How to log in to the web management page

routers.credential_note: Two passwords matter on an Archer C80 and they are not the same thing. The WiFi 5 (802.11ac) network name and key are printed on the underside label. The admin password is not printed anywhere — current Archer firmware makes you invent one at first login, so admin/admin does not apply.
routers.reset_steps: With the router powered on, use a pin to press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back for about 10 seconds until the LEDs blink, then release. The router reboots to factory defaults. Rejoin the default WiFi with the SSID and key from the bottom label, browse to http://tplinkwifi.net or 192.168.0.1, and invent a new admin password when prompted.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — How to log in to the web management page

routers.credential_note: The gaming-line Archer GX90 is a tri-band AX6600 box, and it authenticates like every current Archer: you create the admin password the first time the web UI loads. No factory pair exists. What is preprinted on the bottom label is the wireless network name and its key, which is a different credential.
routers.reset_steps: With power applied, hold the recessed Reset button for about 10 seconds using a pin, letting go when the LEDs blink. The GX90 reboots into factory defaults. Rejoin the default wireless network from the label, open http://tplinkwifi.net or 192.168.0.1, and create the admin password again.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — How to log in to the web management page

routers.credential_note: BE11000 tri-band Wi-Fi 7 whole-home mesh unit, 2.4/5/6 GHz with MLO, four 2.5 Gbps WAN/LAN ports and USB 3.0 per unit — a Wi-Fi 7 tier above the dual-band Deco X50/X55 and distinct from the BE22000 Deco BE85 already covered. App-only setup via the TP-Link Deco app with a TP-Link ID; you create your own Wi-Fi name/password and there is no web-admin default.
routers.reset_steps: Press the Reset button for 1 second and release to reset the Deco to factory defaults (LED changes from pulsing yellow to solid yellow), then re-run setup in the TP-Link Deco app.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Deco BE65 BE11000 Wi-Fi 7 Mesh System User Guide (1910013361) — official

routers.credential_note: BE22000 WiFi 7 mesh. The official install path is the Deco app signed in with a TP-Link ID; no universal default password exists. Web management at tplinkdeco.net (192.168.68.1) uses that same TP-Link ID password.
routers.reset_steps: Use Reset inside the Deco app, or hold the physical Reset button on a Deco unit until the light pulses and set it up again in the app.
routers.source_name: TP-Link official FAQ 2641 (Deco web management access)

routers.credential_note: Deco M4 units are managed the way every Deco is: from the phone app, tied to a TP-Link ID login. No browser-based admin page exists, so no factory admin/admin can exist either. Whoever runs the initial install picks the wireless name and passphrase.
routers.reset_steps: With a pin, depress Reset on the bottom of the node for about a second. The light flashes yellow while clearing, turns steady yellow while restarting, and pulses blue once defaults are restored. Setup then starts over inside the Deco app after you sign in to your TP-Link ID.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — Deco Setup Guide

routers.credential_note: Lists that publish a default admin password for the Deco X20 are describing hardware it does not have. This WiFi 6 node offers no web interface at all — management happens only in the Deco app under a TP-Link ID account, and the wireless name plus its password are ones you pick yourself at install time.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the bottom-mounted Reset button down with a pin for around one second. Yellow flashing shows the erase running, steady yellow covers the restart, and blue pulsing confirms the unit sits at factory defaults again. Re-provisioning means opening the Deco app, signing into your TP-Link ID, and naming the network once more.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — Deco Setup Guide

routers.credential_note: The credential that matters on a Deco X50 is your TP-Link ID, not a router password. Setup, firmware and every setting live inside the Deco phone app; there is no web console to point a browser at. The WiFi 6 network name and passphrase get defined during that first app-guided install.
routers.reset_steps: A pin into the Reset hole on the underside, held for about a second, starts the wipe. The indicator flashes yellow during the reset, goes solid yellow through the reboot, then pulses blue once the node is back at factory defaults. From there the Deco app plus your TP-Link ID re-provisions it from scratch.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — Deco Setup Guide

routers.credential_note: AX3000 dual-band Wi-Fi 6 weatherproof outdoor/indoor mesh unit, 2.4/5 GHz, two gigabit ports with 802.3at PoE or AC power, pole/wall/tabletop mount — the outdoor-rated SKU distinct from the indoor Deco X50 already covered. App-only setup via the TP-Link Deco app with a TP-Link ID; you create your own Wi-Fi credentials and there is no web-admin default.
routers.reset_steps: Press the Reset button for 1 second and release to reset the Deco to factory defaults (light changes from pulsing yellow to solid yellow), then re-run setup in the TP-Link Deco app.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Deco X50-Outdoor AX3000 Outdoor Mesh Wi-Fi 6 User Guide (1910013300) — official

routers.credential_note: Deco X55 is a WiFi 6 mesh node, and nodes in this family expose no browser login page whatsoever. Everything runs through the Deco mobile app, authenticated with a TP-Link ID. No admin/admin exists because no admin console exists; the wireless name and its password are ones you choose while the app walks through setup.
routers.reset_steps: Press the recessed Reset button underneath the unit with a pin and hold roughly one second. Watch the LED: flashing yellow means it is clearing, solid yellow means it is rebooting, and a pulsing blue glow means factory state has been reached. Launch the Deco app, sign in with your TP-Link ID, and build the network again.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — Deco Setup Guide

routers.credential_note: AX3000 mesh set up through the Deco app with a TP-Link ID — there is no device-specific default password. The web console at tplinkdeco.net (192.168.68.1) is secondary and signs in with your TP-Link ID password.
routers.reset_steps: Reset from inside the Deco app, or hold the Reset button on the underside of a Deco unit until its LED pulses, then re-run setup in the Deco app.
routers.source_name: TP-Link official FAQ 2641 (Deco web management access)

routers.credential_note: Tri-band Wi-Fi 6 mesh unit (AX3600-class, dedicated 5GHz backhaul band, 1.5GHz quad-core CPU, 2x gigabit ports per unit) — distinct hardware from the dual-band Deco X55/X60 already covered. Set up through the Deco app with a TP-Link ID; no device-specific default password. Web console at tplinkdeco.net (192.168.68.1) signs in with that same TP-Link ID password.
routers.reset_steps: Reset from inside the Deco app, or hold the Reset button on the underside of a Deco unit until its LED pulses, then re-run setup in the Deco app.
routers.source_name: TP-Link official FAQ 2641 (Deco web management access — applies to Deco X68)

routers.credential_note: AXE11000 tri-band Whole-Home Mesh Wi-Fi 6E (adds the 6 GHz band) system. App-only: setup and administration run through the Deco app with a TP-Link ID — there is no web login host, no username, and no static default password. TP-Link's guide directs you to "Download and install the Deco app" to set up the system.
routers.reset_steps: Press the Reset button for 1 second; the LED changing from pulsing yellow to solid yellow confirms the factory reset. Re-setup is done entirely in the Deco app.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Deco XE200 User Guide REV1.0.0 — official PDF

routers.credential_note: An AXE5400 tri-band node, so the Deco XE75 adds a 6 GHz radio — but its login story matches the rest of the range: no web page, no shipped password. Control is via the Deco app with a TP-Link ID, and you define the SSID and its key during guided setup.
routers.reset_steps: Use a pin on the Reset button beneath the node, holding roughly one second. Flashing yellow signals the clear, solid yellow the reboot, pulsing blue that factory defaults are live. Re-run the guided install in the Deco app with your TP-Link ID to recreate the network.
routers.source_name: TP-Link Official Support — Deco Setup Guide

routers.credential_note: AC1200 Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac Wave 2) dual-band ceiling-mount indoor access point; runs standalone or under an Omada SDN controller. Standalone-mode default admin/admin confirmed by name in TP-Link's official EAP-series login FAQ (forced password change on first login).
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the recessed RESET button for about 5 seconds until the LED blinks, then release and wait for the AP to reboot to factory defaults.
routers.source_name: TP-Link FAQ 1000 — How do I login to the web management page of the EAP Series products (Standalone mode)? (official)

routers.credential_note: Wi-Fi 6 (AX1800) ceiling/wall-mount Omada access point with PoE, standalone or controller-managed — a newer AX-class tier above the AC-class EAP225 already covered. Same official TP-Link EAP-series login FAQ: default username and password are both 'admin' (all lowercase), forced change on first login.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button for about 5 seconds until all LEDs flash, then release to restore factory defaults. Launch a browser to http://tplinkeap.net (or 192.168.0.254 if no DHCP) and log in with admin/admin.
routers.source_name: TP-Link official FAQ 1000 — How do I login to the web management page of the EAP Series products (Standalone mode)? (applies to EAP610)

routers.credential_note: TP-Link's official TL-WR841N (through v14) user guide explicitly states the default username and password are both admin. This is one of the last mainstream models to keep a true admin/admin default — most TP-Link routers from ~2019 onward force you to create a password on first login instead.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser to http://tplinkwifi.net (or http://192.168.0.1) and log in with admin / admin (all lowercase). To factory reset, with the router powered on press and hold the Reset button on the back for about 10 seconds until the LEDs flash, then release; credentials revert to admin / admin.
routers.source_name: TP-Link TL-WR841N V14 User Guide (official)

routers.credential_note: TPG's Nokia FastMile 3.2 fixed-wireless 5G modem (Wi-Fi 6, 5G/4G FWA for TPG Home Wireless Broadband). Username is admin; the admin password is unique per device, printed on the barcode sticker — not a shared static default.
routers.reset_steps: Browse to https://192.168.1.1 and log in with username admin and the default password printed on the modem's barcode sticker. To reset, hold the recessed reset button until the modem restarts to factory defaults, then log in again with the sticker password.
routers.source_name: TPG Support — Basic Wi-Fi settings on a TPG modem (official)

routers.credential_note: Modular open-source router (1GHz dual-core, Turris OS / OpenWrt-based), expandable via MOX B-G modules with Wi-Fi as an mPCIe/SDIO add-on. There is NO default password: the first step of the reForis wizard at http://192.168.1.1 (when MOX runs as DHCP server) has you set the administrative password. Advanced LuCI/SSH uses user 'root'.
routers.reset_steps: Use the rear reset button's LED-count rescue modes; select the factory-reset mode and release to restore defaults and re-run the first-boot wizard.
routers.source_name: Turris Documentation — MOX first setup

routers.credential_note: Open-source dual-band router running Turris OS (OpenWrt-based) with the reForis web admin. There is NO default password: you create the admin password in the first-boot reForis wizard at http://192.168.1.1. reForis login is password-only (no username); the advanced LuCI/SSH interface uses user 'root' with the same password.
routers.reset_steps: Use the rear reset button to select a rescue mode by LED count; holding to the factory-reset count and releasing restores factory defaults and re-triggers the first-boot wizard.
routers.source_name: Turris Documentation — First setup on Turris 1.X and Omnia

routers.credential_note: App-only — no admin/admin default. The admin password is one you set during setup in the AmpliFi app. There is no password recovery, so a lost password means a factory reset.
routers.reset_steps: AmpliFi Alien is administered through the AmpliFi mobile app. To factory reset: use a paperclip to hold the reset button on the bottom of the Alien router for 5 seconds, or until the screen shows 'rebooting', then release (reset MeshPoints first if part of a kit). Set it up again in the AmpliFi app, where you create a new administrator/Wi-Fi password.
routers.source_name: AmpliFi Help Center

routers.credential_note: App-only in practice — no admin/admin default. You create the router password during first-time setup in the AmpliFi app. There is no password recovery; a forgotten password requires a factory reset.
routers.reset_steps: AmpliFi HD is set up and managed in the AmpliFi mobile app (a limited web view exists at amplifi.lan, but there is no admin/admin default). To factory reset the router: use a straightened paperclip to press the reset button on the bottom for 5 seconds, or until the screen shows 'rebooting', then release. Reset any MeshPoints first (hold the reset hole on the side ~10 seconds). Re-run setup in the AmpliFi app and create a new admin/Wi-Fi password.
routers.source_name: AmpliFi Help Center

routers.credential_note: 12-port Gigabit Ethernet router (2x SFP + 10x RJ45), rack-mountable 1U unit running EdgeOS — the highest-port-count model in the EdgeRouter line. Genuine static ubnt/ubnt confirmed in the official quick start guide.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button for about 10 seconds until the front-panel LEDs flash in unison, then release; the router reboots to factory defaults. Connect to eth0, browse to https://192.168.1.1, and log in with ubnt/ubnt.
routers.source_name: Ubiquiti ER-12 (EdgeRouter 12) Quick Start Guide (official)

routers.credential_note: 4-port Gigabit Ethernet router plus one SFP port, EdgeOS on a 1 GHz dual-core CPU with hardware offload, no Wi-Fi. Genuine static ubnt/ubnt out of the box; eth0 is preset to a static 192.168.1.1.
routers.reset_steps: With the router running, press and hold the recessed Reset button until the interface LEDs flash and the unit reboots to defaults. Connect to eth0, browse to https://192.168.1.1, enter ubnt/ubnt, and accept the licence agreement.
routers.source_name: Ubiquiti EdgeRouter ER-4 Quick Start Guide (official)

routers.credential_note: 6-port Gigabit router with 5x PoE-passthrough ports, desktop fanless unit running EdgeOS — built for powering downstream PoE APs/cameras straight from the router. Genuine static ubnt/ubnt confirmed in the official quick start guide.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button for about 10 seconds until the front-panel LEDs flash in unison, then release; the router reboots to factory defaults. Connect to eth0, browse to https://192.168.1.1, and log in with ubnt/ubnt.
routers.source_name: Ubiquiti ER-6P (EdgeRouter 6P) Quick Start Guide (official)

routers.credential_note: 3-port Gigabit Ethernet router, fanless desktop unit with a dual-core MIPS64 CPU running EdgeOS, no Wi-Fi — the entry model in the EdgeRouter line below the ER-X. Genuine static ubnt/ubnt confirmed in the official quick start guide.
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the Reset button for about 10 seconds until the front-panel LEDs flash in unison, then release; the router reboots to factory defaults. Connect to eth0, browse to https://192.168.1.1, and log in with ubnt/ubnt.
routers.source_name: Ubiquiti ERLite-3 (EdgeRouter Lite) Quick Start Guide (official)

routers.credential_note: 5-port Gigabit Ethernet router running EdgeOS, with passive-PoE passthrough, fanless, no Wi-Fi. Genuine static ubnt/ubnt out of the box (eth0 is preset to 192.168.1.1); EdgeOS does not force a password change in its first-login flow.
routers.reset_steps: With the router fully booted, press and hold the Reset button for about 10 seconds until the eth4 LED flashes then goes solid; release and it auto-reboots to defaults. Connect to eth0, browse to https://192.168.1.1, enter ubnt/ubnt, and accept the licence agreement.
routers.source_name: Ubiquiti EdgeRouter ER-X Quick Start Guide (official)

routers.credential_note: Set-on-setup — the UDM has no admin/admin default. You create the administrator credentials (UI Account or local admin) in the setup wizard on first use. After adoption, device-level passwords are randomized by the controller.
routers.reset_steps: There is no universal default password. To set up or recover: reset the UDM by holding the reset button on the bottom for about 10 seconds until the LED changes, releasing when it restarts. Then run the wizard — connect a computer or the UniFi Network mobile app to the same network and go to https://setup.ui.com (Chrome), or browse to the console at https://192.168.1.1, and create your admin login (a UI Account or a local admin) during setup.
routers.source_name: Ubiquiti UDM Quick Start Guide

routers.credential_note: Set-on-setup — there is no admin/admin default on the UDM-Pro. Administrator credentials are created during the first-run wizard; the local console requires the login you set, and adopted UniFi devices get randomized passwords.
routers.reset_steps: No factory admin password exists. To set up or regain access: hold the reset button on the front until the device restarts to factory defaults, then launch Chrome and go to https://setup.ui.com (or connect the UniFi Network mobile app), on the same LAN as the UDM-Pro. Follow the Setup Wizard and create your own admin login (UI Account or local admin). Locally you can then reach the console at https://192.168.1.1.
routers.source_name: Ubiquiti UDM-Pro Quick Start Guide

routers.credential_note: No default admin password. Setup forces you to create a local admin and/or sign in with a Ubiquiti account; those credentials are the only way in. SSH is disabled by default. There is no ubnt/ubnt web login on modern UniFi consoles.
routers.reset_steps: Power on the UDM-SE and run the setup wizard from the UniFi mobile app (over Bluetooth/Wi-Fi) or from a browser at http://192.168.1.1 or unifi.ui.com. During setup you either sign in with a Ubiquiti (UI.com) account or create a local administrator username and password — that becomes your login. To factory reset, hold the recessed Reset button for about 10 seconds until the LED changes, then re-run the setup wizard.
routers.source_name: Ubiquiti Help Center (How to Set Up UniFi)

routers.credential_note: No universal admin/password — a UI.com cloud account is created/used during UniFi OS setup (or set up via the UniFi app). Default gateway 192.168.1.1.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the RESET button ~10 seconds until the LED changes to restore factory defaults.
routers.source_name: Ubiquiti Help Center — How to Set Up UniFi

routers.credential_note: A UniFi access point is not logged into directly with a password. It is adopted into a UniFi controller/app, where you set the admin account. There is no per-AP admin/admin web login.
routers.reset_steps: The U6 Lite has no standalone web admin — it is adopted and managed by a UniFi Network controller (a UniFi console like a Dream Machine, or the self-hosted UniFi Network application) using the UniFi app. Plug the AP in, open the UniFi app, and adopt it; your admin credentials live on the controller, not the AP. To factory reset, hold the recessed Reset button for about 10 seconds until the LED flashes, then re-adopt it.
routers.source_name: Ubiquiti Help Center (How to Set Up UniFi)

routers.credential_note: Askey-made 5G/LTE fixed-wireless home gateway for Verizon 5G Home Internet (LV55/LVSKIHP variants) — a fixed-wireless unit distinct from the Fios fibre routers G3100/CR1000A already covered. Password-only Web GUI login (no username), activated via the My Verizon app. Verizon: "You can find the default password on the label under the 5G Internet Gateway."
routers.reset_steps: Reset to factory defaults from the admin Web GUI, or use the security questions set during setup to revert the admin password. If forgotten, the label password under the unit is the factory default; default LAN IP is 192.168.0.1.
routers.source_name: Verizon 5G Internet Gateway User Guide — official PDF

routers.credential_note: The G3100 uses username 'admin' plus a per-device Administrator Password printed on the rear label — there is no shared default password. The admin password on the label is separate from the WiFi password (also on the label).
routers.reset_steps: Browse to http://myfiosgateway.com or http://192.168.1.1. Sign in with username 'admin' and the unique Administrator Password printed on the label on the back of the G3100. To factory reset, press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back ~15 seconds until the router restarts, then log in with the label's admin password.
routers.source_name: Verizon Internet Support — Fios Router

routers.credential_note: Askey model NCM1100 LTE fixed-wireless home gateway (NCM1100E is the business variant) for Verizon LTE Home Internet — managed at mynetworksettings.com or 192.168.1.1, distinct from the 5G ASK-NCQ1338 gateway and the LTE Home Router in this run. Password-only login (no username). Verizon: "enter the password that is printed next to the Password on the label on the back of the Gateway."
routers.reset_steps: Use the reset button to restore factory defaults; the password printed next to 'Password' on the rear label is the factory default, and the factory Wi-Fi uses a unique WPA2 key on the rear sticker.
routers.source_name: Verizon Internet Gateway (ASK-NCM1100) User Manual v1 — official PDF

routers.credential_note: Dual-band Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac) LTE fixed-wireless home router for Verizon LTE Home Internet, broadcasting LTE-Home-xxxx SSIDs (2.4G + 5G) — distinct from the 5G ASK-NCQ1338 gateway and the Fios routers already covered. Password-only login (no username). Verizon: "Log in using the default password (Check your router's product label for your unique GUI Password)."
routers.reset_steps: Press and hold the reset button on the router to restore factory defaults; the unique GUI password on the product label is the factory default. Manage at http://192.168.1.1.
routers.source_name: Verizon LTE Home Router User Guide — official PDF

routers.credential_note: Like the G3100, the CR1000A ships with username 'admin' and a unique Administrator Password on the rear label — no universal default. The admin password differs from the WiFi/network password shown on the same label.
routers.reset_steps: Open a browser to http://myfiosgateway.com or http://192.168.1.1 and sign in with username 'admin' and the Administrator Password printed on the label on the back of the CR1000A. To factory reset, press and hold the recessed Reset button ~15 seconds until the router reboots, then log in with the label's admin password.
routers.source_name: Verizon Support — Verizon Router (CR1000A) Overview

routers.credential_note: App-only — Vilo does not expose a web admin interface. There is no admin/admin default. The Wi-Fi name and password printed on the bottom label are only used to join the pod during app setup; you set your own network password in the app.
routers.reset_steps: Vilo has no 192.168.x.x web login — configuration is done entirely in the Vilo mobile app. To factory reset: use a paperclip or pin to press and hold the reset button on the back of the Vilo for about 6 seconds until the light on the front flashes red. Then add the Vilo back in the app; the default network name and password used to join during setup are printed on the bottom of the pod.
routers.source_name: Vilo Living Support

routers.credential_note: No universal default. Each Hub 3 ships with a unique settings password printed on the base label (shown separately from the WiFi password). Logging in requires only that printed settings password.
routers.reset_steps: To log in: connect to the hub, browse to 192.168.0.1 and enter the settings password. The settings password is printed on a sticker on the base of the hub, labelled 'Settings password' — this is not your WiFi password. To factory reset: with the hub switched on, use a pen to press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back/base for 10 seconds, then wait a few minutes for the white power light to become solidly lit; all settings revert to the values printed on the base.
routers.source_name: Virgin Media Help — Reboot or reset your Hub

routers.credential_note: No universal default. Each Hub 4 ships with a unique settings password on the base label, separate from the WiFi password. This is the whole login — there is no admin/admin.
routers.reset_steps: To log in: connect to the hub, browse to 192.168.0.1 and enter the settings password printed on the base of the hub (labelled 'Settings password', different from the WiFi password). To factory reset: with the hub powered on, use a pen to press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back/base for 10 seconds, then wait a few minutes until the white front power light is solidly lit; all custom settings are wiped back to the base-label values.
routers.source_name: Virgin Media Help — Reboot or reset your Hub

routers.credential_note: No universal default. Each Hub 5 ships with a unique settings password printed on the base, distinct from the WiFi password. Aggregator 'admin/admin' listings are wrong for this device.
routers.reset_steps: To log in: connect to the hub, browse to 192.168.0.1 and enter the settings password from the base label (labelled 'Settings password', not the WiFi password). To factory reset: with the hub on, use a pen to press and hold the recessed Reset button on the back/base for 10 seconds, then wait a few minutes for the white power light to become solid; all settings return to the base-label defaults.
routers.source_name: Virgin Media Help — Reboot or reset your Hub

routers.credential_note: Recent Vodafone hubs (e.g. THG3000) do not use admin/admin — the admin password is a unique value printed on the base/back label, and you are forced to change it after first login.
routers.reset_steps: To log in: connect to the hub, browse to 192.168.1.1, use username 'admin' and the unit-specific admin password printed on the sticker on the base/back of the hub. You are prompted to change it on first login. To factory reset: with the hub on, press and hold the recessed Reset pinhole on the back for about 10 seconds until it reboots; the admin password returns to the printed default.
routers.source_name: Vodafone UK Support — How do I manage my Vodafone router settings?

routers.credential_note: DOCSIS cable gateway issued by Vodafone Germany for cable broadband plans. Admin UI at 192.168.0.1 with username admin; the password is device-unique, printed on the rear label and on the bundled WLAN card — not a shared static default, per Vodafone's own support page.
routers.reset_steps: Insert a pointed object into the recessed RESET button and hold for at least 30 seconds; the Vodafone Station automatically performs a factory reset and restarts.
routers.source_name: Vodafone Deutschland — Hilfe: Vodafone Station (official)

routers.credential_note: FTTH/FTTC fibre gateway issued by Vodafone Italy. Both the router Username and Password (distinct from the Wi-Fi key) are printed on a per-unit label under the base — accessed at vodafone.station / 192.168.1.1. Vodafone Italia: "il nome Utente e la Password Router che trovi sull'etichetta che trovi sotto la base della tua Vodafone Power Station."
routers.reset_steps: Hold the reset button at least 5 seconds to restore factory settings; the router Username and Password are printed on the label under the base of the unit.
routers.source_name: Vodafone Italia — assistenza dispositivi (Vodafone Power Station)

routers.credential_note: Wi-Fi 6 FTTH/FTTC fibre gateway issued by Vodafone Italy — the newer Wi-Fi 6 hardware, with its label on the side (vs under the base on the Power Station). Router Username and Password (distinct from the Wi-Fi key) are per-unit on that label. Vodafone Italia: "il nome Utente e la Password Router che trovi sull'etichetta che trovi lateralmente sulla tua Vodafone WiFi 6 Station."
routers.reset_steps: Restore factory settings via the reset button; the router Username and Password are printed on the label on the side of the unit.
routers.source_name: Vodafone Italia — assistenza dispositivi (Vodafone Wi-Fi 6 Station)

routers.credential_note: Wavlink's official docs state a genuine factory default: the web login password is 'admin' (password-only, no username) at 192.168.10.1 / wavlogin.link. This universal default is a real security risk - change it right after setup.
routers.reset_steps: Reset: press and hold the RESET button with a pin for about 8-15 seconds until the device reboots, then release. Browse to http://192.168.10.1 or http://wavlogin.link, log in with the password admin, and change it immediately.
routers.source_name: Wavlink Official FAQ - How to log into the web-based management page of my WAVLINK router

routers.credential_note: There is no universal admin/password on current XB7 firmware. Username is 'admin' but the default password is the unique code printed on the device label, and newer builds also require you to switch on Admin Tool access from the Xfinity app before 10.0.0.1 will load.
routers.reset_steps: Log in to the Admin Tool by opening a browser to http://10.0.0.1 and signing in with username 'admin'. On XB7 firmware you may first need to enable web access: open the Xfinity app > WiFi > View WiFi equipment > Advanced Settings > Admin Tool online access > turn ON. The initial Admin Tool password is the unique value printed on the sticker on the side/bottom of the gateway (it is NOT 'password' on current firmware). To factory reset, press and hold the recessed Reset pinhole on the back for ~30 seconds until the gateway reboots, then log in with the sticker credentials.
routers.source_name: Xfinity Support — Change your WiFi with the Gateway Admin Tool

routers.credential_note: No admin/admin or admin/password default on the XB8. The label carries a unique admin password, and web admin access often has to be toggled on from the Xfinity app first because WiFi Intelligence locks the local tool.
routers.reset_steps: Browse to http://10.0.0.1 and sign in with username 'admin'. If the page won't load, enable it first in the Xfinity app: WiFi > View WiFi equipment > Advanced Settings > Admin Tool online access > ON. The default Admin Tool password is the unique string on the label on the bottom of the XB8 (not 'password'). Factory reset: hold the recessed Reset pinhole on the rear ~30 seconds until it reboots; log back in with the label credentials.
routers.source_name: Xfinity Support — Change your WiFi with the Gateway Admin Tool

routers.credential_note: The Mi Router 4A Gigabit Edition answers on 192.168.31.1 and has no shared default. Whoever runs initial setup — through router.miwifi.com, the Mi Home app, or the older Mi WiFi app — creates the management password, and there is no username to go with it.
routers.reset_steps: With the router on, hold the Reset button on the bottom until the indicator light changes/blinks (~5–10 seconds) to restore factory settings.
routers.source_name: Xiaomi Mi Router 4A Gigabit Edition official User Guide

routers.credential_note: AX3000T is Xiaomi's AX3000 WiFi 6 router. It carries no universal password: the management password is one you choose the first time you set the unit up, either at router.miwifi.com or from the Mi Home app.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button underneath the powered router until the indicator light changes or blinks — roughly 5-10 seconds — to return it to factory settings.
routers.source_name: Xiaomi Router AX3000T official FAQ (mi.com)

routers.credential_note: Ziply Fiber's Arris/CommScope NVG448BQ fibre gateway (Wi-Fi 6, XGS-PON FTTH, multi-gig). The web admin at 192.168.254.254 is protected by a per-device 10-digit Device Access Code on the bottom bar-code label — not a shared admin/admin default; login is code-only with no username.
routers.reset_steps: Enter 192.168.254.254 in a browser and log in with the 10-digit Device Access Code printed on the bar-code sticker on the bottom of the router. To reset, hold the router's reset button to restore the factory settings (SSID/password/access code) shown on the sticker.
routers.source_name: Ziply Fiber Help Center — Change the name and password of your home network (official)

routers.credential_note: No password required for the first login; you set the admin password during initial setup. No default username.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the Reset button ~5–10 seconds until the LED responds to restore factory defaults.
routers.source_name: Zyxel Armor G5 (NBG7815) official User's Guide

routers.credential_note: AX1800 mesh managed via the Zyxel Multy app. There is no static admin default: the web GUI at 192.168.212.1 uses either a myZyxelCloud account or a local password you create during app registration. The label SSID/key is for Wi-Fi, not admin.
routers.reset_steps: Hold the RESET button on the Multy unit about 5 seconds until the LED changes, then reconfigure through the Zyxel Multy app.
routers.source_name: Zyxel official Multy WiFi online help

routers.credential_note: App-only. The Multy X is set up and administered through the Zyxel Multy mobile app; there is no admin/admin web default. Your credentials are the Wi-Fi password you set in the app and, optionally, a myZyxelCloud account.
routers.reset_steps: The Multy X is managed with the Zyxel Multy app (optionally signed into a myZyxelCloud account) — there is no traditional web login. To factory reset a unit: use a paperclip or toothpick to press and hold the reset button in the small hole next to the power jack for about 5 seconds; the LED starts fast-blinking red to show it is resetting. Then re-add the unit in the Zyxel Multy app and set your Wi-Fi name and password.
routers.source_name: Zyxel Multy X User's Guide

routers.credential_note: Per the official user's guide you sign in with username admin and a randomly-assigned default password printed on the device label — unique per unit, not a shared default — and are prompted to change it at first login.
routers.reset_steps: With the device on, insert a thin pin into the RESET hole and hold until it reboots to reload the factory-default configuration, then log in with the label password.
routers.source_name: Zyxel official NBG7510 User's Guide (V1.00 Ed6)

routers.credential_note: Business Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) AX1800 dual-radio 2x2 PoE access point in the NebulaFlex line — runs standalone or under Nebula cloud (NCC). Genuine documented static default admin/1234 for the local Web Configurator at 192.168.1.2. When adopted by Nebula the credential is set in NCC instead.
routers.reset_steps: Ceiling/wall-mount AP powered by 802.3af/at PoE. Restore factory defaults (reset button or Web Configurator), then browse to the DHCP-assigned IP or http://192.168.1.2 and sign in with admin / 1234; the Update Admin Info screen then forces a new password.
routers.source_name: Zyxel NWA110AX User's Guide (V6.60) — download.zyxel.com (official)

routers.credential_note: Business Wi-Fi 6 AX3000 access point with a 4x4:4 (5GHz) plus 2x2:2 (2.4GHz) radio design and 802.3at PoE+ input, part of the NebulaFlex family (standalone or Nebula cloud). Documented static default admin/1234 on the local Web Configurator; when the AP is Nebula-managed (NCC) the login lives in the cloud account.
routers.reset_steps: Higher-tier PoE+ AP for dense deployments. After a factory reset, reach it at its DHCP-assigned address or http://192.168.1.2 and log in with admin / 1234; the wizard then prompts for a new admin password.
routers.source_name: Zyxel NWA210AX User's Guide (V6.55) — download.zyxel.com (official)

routers.credential_note: Username is admin, but the password is the unique value printed on the device label — not a shared default. Zyxel access points made before Feb 2025 used a static '1234'; newer models ship with the per-device label password and no universal default.
routers.reset_steps: Connect to the AP and browse to http://192.168.1.1 (or the IP it received from your router). Log in with username 'admin' and the randomly assigned password printed on the device label. If the unit is older (manufactured before Feb 2025), the default password is '1234'. To factory reset, hold the Reset button for about 10 seconds until the LEDs blink and the AP reboots, then log in with the label password (or 1234 on older units).
routers.source_name: Zyxel Support Campus EMEA (default password on Zyxel access points)

routers.credential_note: 802.11ax dual-radio PoE unified access point in the NWA50/90/55 series — a distinct model from the already-covered NWA110AX/NWA210AX. Official user guide: 'Enter the user name (default: "admin") and password (default: "1234")' — same static-default precedent as its NebulaFlex siblings.
routers.reset_steps: Press the RESET button for more than 5 seconds to return to factory defaults, then browse to http://192.168.1.2 and log in with admin/1234 — the Update Admin Info screen then forces a new password.
routers.source_name: Zyxel NWA50/90/55 Series User's Guide V6.29 Ed2 — download.zyxel.com (official)

routers.credential_note: Compact UOS-based security gateway/firewall (USG FLEX H series) — Zyxel's newest gateway line, distinct from the older ZyWALL-based USG FLEX and from the NWA-series access points already covered. Official user guide cover page: 'Login IP Address https://192.168.168.1 / User Name admin / Password See Zyxel Device label or 1234.'
routers.reset_steps: Press the RESET button for more than 5 seconds to restore factory defaults, then browse to https://192.168.168.1 and log in with admin/1234 (or the password on the device label, if present); a new password is forced immediately after.
routers.source_name: Zyxel USG FLEX H Series User's Guide V1.30 Ed1 — download.zyxel.com (official)

routers.credential_note: NebulaFlex PRO dual-radio 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) unified access point (4x4-class 5 GHz); standalone, Nebula (NCC), or AC managed. In standalone mode it ships the genuine static default admin / 1234. Zyxel: "Enter the user name (default: 'admin') and password (default: '1234')."
routers.reset_steps: Hold the physical Reset button to restore factory defaults. In standalone mode, browse to http://1.1.1.1 (initial setup) or the device IP http://192.168.1.2 and log in with admin / 1234; the Update Admin Info screen then prompts a password change.
routers.source_name: Zyxel WAX610D User's Guide V6.70 — official PDF
